classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_source
items.description:
Toroidal component of the area-normalized net momentum-transfer source for a
specified neutral internal state, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source term for a
neutral internal state is the signed projection of the state-resolved net
momentum-transfer source onto the local toroidal direction. It represents
the toroidal part of the area-normalized momentum exchange between that
neutral internal state and the plasma or other interacting populations.

The component is defined by projection onto the toroidal unit vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame:

$$
S_{\phi,n,\alpha} = \mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi
$$

where $S_{\phi,n,\alpha}$ is the toroidal momentum-source component,
$\mathbf{S}_{n,\alpha}$ is the area-normalized vector momentum source for
neutral species $n$ in internal state $\alpha$, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi$
is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.
Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
coordinate.

This quantity is resolved for the specified neutral internal state:
contributions from other neutral internal states are excluded, and no sum
over neutral internal states is implied. It applies to the edge-plasma
momentum exchange and uses the net source rather than an individual transfer
process.

This component is derived from the vector [neutral state momentum
source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source). It is distinct from
the state-summed [toroidal neutral momentum
source](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_source), which combines the
corresponding toroidal contributions from all neutral internal states, and
from the field-aligned [parallel neutral state momentum
source](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_source), which uses a different
projection direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the area-normalized net momentum-transfer
source for the specified neutral internal state has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density
items.description:
Local ratio of tritium-ion to deuterium-ion number densities, expressing
fuel-isotope composition independently of the total fuel-ion density.
items.documentation:
The local tritium-to-deuterium density ratio expresses the relative
abundance of the two hydrogen-isotope fuel-ion populations at the same
location. It is derived from the local [tritium
density](name:tritium_density) and [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density).

$$
R_{T/D} = \frac{n_T}{n_D}
$$

where $R_{T/D}$ is the tritium-to-deuterium density ratio, and $n_T$ and
$n_D$ are the local number densities of tritium and deuterium ions,
respectively. The densities include the relevant isotope populations summed
over their charge states unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is
explicitly specified.

This ratio is dimensionless and does not represent the total fuel-ion
density; multiplying it by the deuterium density gives the tritium density.

items.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity
items.description:
Toroidal current density due to heat viscosity is the signed charge flux
around the symmetry axis generated by heat-viscosity stresses in a
collisional magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density due to heat viscosity is the geometric-toroidal
component of the electric-current contribution generated by heat-viscosity
stresses in a collisional magnetized-plasma fluid closure.

Its defining projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
is

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal current density due to heat viscosity,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{hv}}$ is the [heat-viscosity current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. Here $R$ is the major
radius measured from the symmetry axis, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local, unaveraged contribution to [electric current
density](name:current_density), not a surface-integrated current or the
total current density from all mechanisms. Only the heat-viscosity
contribution is included; the definition imposes no restriction to a
particular plasma region.

Unlike [parallel current density due to heat
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity), which
projects the same parent vector along the local magnetic field, this
quantity projects onto the geometric toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the heat-viscosity current flows in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: minor_angle_of_pellet_injector
items.description:
Minor directional half-opening angle of the elliptic fragment-dispersion
cone formed by a shattered pellet injector.
items.documentation:
Minor half-opening angle of the elliptic shatter cone formed by a shattered
pellet injector is the angular separation between the cone axis and its
boundary along the minor transverse semi-axis. It is the minor directional
component of the angle of the pellet injector.

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{minor}} = \arccos\left(\hat{u}_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}\right)
$$

where $\alpha_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the minor half-opening angle,
$\hat{u}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the shatter-cone axis unit vector, and
$\hat{u}_{\mathrm{minor}}$ is the unit vector along the cone's minor
semi-axis. The quantity describes a half-angle, not the full angular
opening; the corresponding major-direction value is the major angle of the
pellet injector.

items.name: total_ion_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Charge-state-summed number density of all ion species in the boundary plasma
immediately on the plasma-facing side of a limiter surface.
items.documentation:
Total ion density at a limiter is the local number density of all charged
ion species and ionization states at the plasma-side evaluation point
adjacent to the limiter. It is the charge-state-summed component of
ion_density_at_limiter.

The defining aggregation is

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state
$Z$, and the sums include every ion species and positive charge state
present at the evaluation point.

Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded, as is electron density. The
limiter-local aggregation is distinct from the corresponding total quantity
at the plasma boundary,
[total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary),
because the evaluation locus is specifically the plasma-facing side of a
limiter surface.

items.name: plasma_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Vector Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive plasma
momentum flux to the local plasma momentum-density gradient, abstracting
over charged plasma constituents, ion charge states, and directional
projections in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Plasma momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive plasma momentum flux and the negative local gradient of plasma
momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum
balance. It describes effective redistribution of aggregate charged-particle
momentum by collisional, neoclassical, turbulent, and drift-related
transport processes. As a direction-dependent vector coefficient, its
components represent anisotropic momentum transport along selected
directions or projections in a magnetized plasma.

The diffusive plasma momentum flux component along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is

$$
\Gamma_{g,i}^{p} = -D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}\frac{\partial g_i^{p}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}$ is the plasma momentum diffusivity component
along $\hat{e}_i$, $\Gamma_{g,i}^{p}$ is the diffusive flux of the plasma
momentum-density component in that direction, $g_i^{p}$ is the aggregate
plasma momentum-density component, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along
$\hat{e}_i$. The negative sign encodes down-gradient diffusion: when
$D_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{p}$ is positive, the diffusive flux opposes the local
momentum-density gradient in that direction.

The aggregate plasma momentum density is formed from charged plasma
constituents, including electrons and ions; ion contributions are summed
over all charge states before the closure is applied, so this quantity is
distinct from an [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity). This parent name
abstracts over plasma-scoped specializations such as [edge plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity) and directional
components such as [vertical plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity), where vertical
denotes the $\hat{Z}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. It excludes neutral-fluid momentum diffusivity.

items.name: total_momentum_flux
items.description:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic pressure, and viscous
stress contributions from any species or population.
items.documentation:
The [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) describes the rate at which linear
momentum crosses a unit area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It
encompasses convective ram pressure, isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous
or turbulent stress contributions from the selected plasma populations.

The momentum-flux tensor for a fluid or aggregated population is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho\,\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is the bulk flow velocity,
$p$ is the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}$ is the viscous or turbulent stress tensor. The momentum
current through a surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This structural quantity is independent of species, population, and
directional projection. Contributions may be aggregated over charged or
neutral populations; [toroidal total momentum
flux](name:toroidal_total_momentum_flux) is a representative directional
projection that combines the total edge-plasma contributions.

items.name: thickness_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Physical thickness of a Bragg crystal is the normal material thickness
measured between its opposing surfaces along the local surface normal. It
excludes the X-ray ray-path length through the crystal, which depends on
incidence geometry.
items.documentation:
Physical thickness of a Bragg crystal is the geometric separation of its
opposing crystal surfaces measured along the local surface normal. It is a
property of the crystal body, independent of the direction taken by an
incident or diffracted X-ray ray.

The local normal thickness is defined by

$$
t = \left| (\mathbf{x}_2 - \mathbf{x}_1) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}} \right|
$$

where $t$ is the Bragg-crystal thickness in meters, $\mathbf{x}_1$ and
$\mathbf{x}_2$ are corresponding points on the two opposing crystal surfaces
in meters, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal to the local surface at
$\mathbf{x}_1$.

This quantity excludes the oblique material path length of an X-ray through
the crystal; for an ideal flat slab that path length also depends on the ray
angle relative to the local normal. It is distinct from
[bragg_crystal_width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_bragg_crystal)
and height_of_bragg_crystal, which are tangential dimensions of the crystal
element.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Density-weighted kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge states
evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode pedestal.
items.documentation:
Ion average temperature at the pedestal top is the density-weighted kinetic
temperature of the combined ion population at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode pedestal. It is the ion-specific component of average temperature at
the pedestal top.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_{i,\mathrm{avg}}$ is the ion average temperature, $n_s$ is the
number density of ion species or charge state $s$, and $T_s$ is its kinetic
temperature. The sum includes all ion species and charge states in the
defined ion population; it is not an electron temperature or a temperature
for a single ion species. The weighting denominator is the total ion density
represented by total ion density at the pedestal top.

items.name: absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor
items.description:
Net radiative power retained by all divertor targets, obtained by
subtracting reflected radiation from incident radiation and summing over the
targets.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net radiative power absorbed by the complete set of
divertor target surfaces during plasma–wall interaction. It represents
incident radiation retained by the targets, rather than radiation that is
merely incident or reflected.

For target surfaces indexed by $k$, the net absorbed radiative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = \sum_{k=1}^{N_t} \left(P_{\mathrm{inc,rad},k} - P_{\mathrm{refl,rad},k}\right)
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the total absorbed radiative power, $N_t$ is
the number of divertor target surfaces, $P_{\mathrm{inc,rad},k}$ is the
radiative power incident on target $k$, and $P_{\mathrm{refl,rad},k}$ is the
radiative power reflected from target $k$.

The quantity is aggregated over all divertor targets and includes only the
radiative contribution. It excludes nonradiative particle and conductive
power included in [total incident power of the
divertor](name:total_incident_power_of_divertor), and it is distinct from
[thermal radiative power of the
divertor](name:thermal_radiative_power_of_divertor), which describes
radiation emitted by the target surfaces. The corresponding per-target
quantity is [absorbed radiated power at divertor
target](name:absorbed_radiated_power_at_divertor_target).

items.name: ion_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective advective ion transport velocity whose product with ion number
density gives the convective particle flux, excluding
density-gradient-driven diffusion.
items.documentation:
Ion particle convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of the
density-proportional advective ion particle flux. It represents directed
particle transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been
separated.

The convective ion particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i\mathbf{v}_i
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective ion particle
flux, $n_i$ is the number density of the specified ion population, and
$\mathbf{v}_i$ is its particle convection velocity; the subscript $i$
denotes ions.

For a specified ion species, the density is summed over all ionic charge
states, excluding neutral particles, and the velocity is the
density-weighted mean over all charge states rather than a sum of
velocities. The [ion charge-state particle convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_particle_convection_velocity) instead
applies to a specified charge state. This quantity describes particle
transport, not heat or momentum transport, and need not equal the ion fluid
velocity. It is not restricted to the edge plasma or to a particular
transport direction.

The [parallel ion particle convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_particle_convection_velocity) is its
magnetic-field-aligned projection. The [radial ion particle convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity) is its major-radius
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
[effective ion particle convection
velocity](name:effective_ion_particle_convection_velocity) specializes to
transport across magnetic flux surfaces; that direction need not coincide
with the cylindrical radial direction.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected convection velocity points along
its defining positive direction: toward increasing $R$ for the cylindrical
radial component, or along the magnetic field for the parallel component.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Non-negative radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface
coinciding with the internal transport barrier, derived from enclosed
toroidal magnetic flux rather than geometric distance.
items.documentation:
The toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport barrier is the
non-negative, radius-like label of the nested magnetic flux surface on which
the barrier is located. It identifies the barrier by magnetic-surface
position and is not a direct geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux:

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the
associated magnetic surface, $B_0$ is the positive reference toroidal
magnetic field, and $\pi$ is the mathematical circle constant.

The locus is the internal transport barrier, represented as a particular
nested magnetic flux surface rather than the entire plasma or a finite
transport-barrier region. This quantity has no species or charge-state
aggregation and is not a spatial average or an integral over a region.

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate). Unlike the [normalized
toroidal-flux coordinate at the internal transport
barrier](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier),
it retains the radius-like coordinate scale rather than applying boundary
normalization.

items.name: torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
items.description:
Vector torque associated with angular momentum carried away by neutral beam
particles that traverse the plasma without ionization. It represents the
shinethrough contribution to the neutral-beam momentum balance, with
components giving the direction and sense of the loss.
items.documentation:
Torque due to neutral beam shinethrough is the vector rate at which angular
momentum is carried out of the plasma by injected neutral particles that
traverse the plasma without ionization or absorption. It is a loss term for
plasma angular momentum because the angular momentum of those unabsorbed
particles is not deposited in the plasma.

The shinethrough torque is defined as the time rate of angular momentum
carried by the shinethrough neutral-particle population:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}} = \frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough and $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the angular momentum
carried by neutral beam particles after they pass through the plasma without
ionization.

This vector quantity is the parent of component quantities such as the
[toroidal torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough](name:toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough), which
is its toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. It excludes angular momentum deposited by absorbed neutral beam
particles and torques due to other momentum-transfer mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{st}}$ is directed along the positive basis
direction of that component; the toroidal component is positive in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing
orbit class. Positive values indicate net addition; negative values indicate
net removal.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the co-passing
orbit class. Co-passing particles are passing particles whose guiding-center
toroidal circulation is in the plasma-current direction.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \left\langle s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} - s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the co-passing thermal particle
source rate, $s_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the local rate of
thermal-particle addition, $s_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{co,th}}$ is the
local rate of thermal-particle removal, $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes
averaging over a magnetic flux surface, and $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux
label of that surface.

The quantity applies only to the thermal population on co-passing, untrapped
passing orbits and is aggregated by flux-surface averaging. Positive values
represent a net source to this orbit class, while negative values represent
a net sink. It excludes trapped and counter-passing orbit populations and
describes particle-number transfer rather than energy or momentum transfer.

This is one orbit-class contribution to the broader [thermal particle source
rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which aggregates source and sink
contributions over the thermal orbit populations. The [counter-passing
thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) is the
corresponding orbit-class contribution for particles circulating opposite to
the plasma-current direction.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex toroidal component of the first-order plasma
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier mode
in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the complex plasma magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the projection $\delta B_\phi =
\delta\mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{\phi}$ along the toroidal unit vector
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This
imaginary part, $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$, together with the [real
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), fully
specifies the complex toroidal component of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic-field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) eigenfunction
associated with a single toroidal mode number $n$ within the confined plasma
region.

The full complex toroidal amplitude is decomposed as:

$$
\delta B_\phi = \mathrm{Re}(\delta B_\phi) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)
$$

where the ratio of imaginary to real parts encodes the spatial phase of the
perturbation relative to the chosen eigenmode gage convention. The absolute
magnitude of the eigenfunction is normalization-dependent and is set by the
stability solver's normalization choice.

This quantity is defined within the confined plasma region and is computed
alongside
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part)
and radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part to fully
characterize the phase-resolved perturbed magnetic-field vector inside the
plasma. The vacuum-region counterpart for the same toroidal component is
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part).

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi)$ is directed
along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: stray_breakdown_magnetic_field
items.description:
Residual magnetic-field strength at the plasma position during initiation,
produced by imperfect cancelation of external coil fields and capable of
inhibiting electron-avalanche breakdown.
items.documentation:
This quantity denotes the residual magnetic-field contribution present at
the plasma position during plasma initiation. It arises when external coil
fields are not completely canceled and is relevant because residual field
can inhibit the electron avalanche required for breakdown.

It is the stray contribution to the [breakdown magnetic
field](name:breakdown_magnetic_field), rather than the complete field
describing the initiation state. The associated [stray breakdown
magnetic-field magnitude](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude)
provides the Euclidean magnitude when a direction-independent measure is
required; this parent quantity does not by itself specify a field direction.

items.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex first-order electrostatic potential
perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear
MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the perturbed electrostatic potential eigenfunction is
one of two real-valued components that together fully specify the complex
scalar perturbation $\delta\phi$ throughout the confined plasma for a single
linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenmode. The irrotational component of the
perturbed electric field is $\delta\mathbf{E}_\mathrm{es} =
-\nabla\delta\phi$, separate from the inductive contribution arising from
the perturbed magnetic vector potential.

The complex eigenfunction decomposes as:

$$
\delta\phi = \operatorname{Re}(\delta\phi) + i\,\operatorname{Im}(\delta\phi)
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}(\delta\phi)$ is the [real
part](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_real_part) and
$\operatorname{Im}(\delta\phi)$ — this quantity — encodes the spatial phase
distribution of the electrostatic perturbation for toroidal mode number $n$.

Linear MHD or extended-MHD stability solvers compute $\delta\phi$ as part of
the eigenmode solution for a specified $n$; the overall complex
normalization is fixed by the solver's phase convention, so the imaginary
part carries physical meaning only in conjunction with the real part. The
same complex decomposition pattern applies to
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part)
within the complete set of MHD perturbation eigenfunctions for the same
eigenmode.

items.name: velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift
velocity produced by crossed local electric and magnetic fields in a
magnetized plasma; it is a speed, not a signed projection along a named
axis. For magnetized charged species this drift is independent of particle
mass and charge sign.
items.documentation:
Velocity due to E cross B drift is the nonnegative magnitude of the drift
velocity arising from crossed electric and magnetic fields in a magnetized
plasma. Because the underlying drift depends only on the local field ratio,
it is identical for all magnetized charged species regardless of particle
mass or charge sign, and the drift by itself carries no net current.

The defining relation is:

$$
v_{E\times B} = \frac{|\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}|}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector. The underlying drift vector
$\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|^2$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$
and has no component along the magnetic-field direction; consequently any
parallel projection of this drift vanishes identically.

This quantity is the speed of the drift and is therefore nonnegative; it
must not be confused with signed axis-resolved projections of the drift
vector, such as the toroidal projection for a specific ion charge state in
[toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
or the parallel projection for a neutral internal state in
[parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
Population-resolved counterparts of the same drift family are provided for
individual ion charge states in
[ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
for internal states in internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift, and
for neutral-species internal states in
neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift.

items.name: ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density
items.description:
Local ion concentration relative to the electron population, defined as the
number-density ratio for a specified impurity or fuel ion species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local abundance of a specified impurity or fuel ion
species relative to the free-electron population. It compares particle
populations rather than electric charge density or mass density.

The local ion-to-electron concentration ratio is defined by

$$
\mathcal{R}_{i/e} = \frac{n_i}{n_e}
$$

where $\mathcal{R}_{i/e}$ is the ion-to-electron concentration ratio, $n_i$
is the local number density of the specified ion species, $n_e$ is the local
free-electron number density, $i$ identifies the selected ion species, and
$e$ identifies the electron population.

Both densities are evaluated at the same local plasma point. For a
species-level numerator without an explicitly selected charge state, $n_i$
is summed over all ionization states of that species; a
charge-state-resolved numerator applies only to the selected state. No
spatial average or line integration is implied.

The numerator is supplied by the corresponding [ion
density](name:ion_density), while [ion charge state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) represents the density when one
charge state is isolated. A named-species example of the same construction
is the [ratio of iron density to electron
density](name:ratio_of_iron_density_to_electron_density). This quantity is
distinct from an ion charge-state fraction, electric charge-density ratio,
or mass-density ratio.

items.name: temperature_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Absolute thermodynamic temperature of a neutron detector assembly or
converter material, describing its thermal state independently of
neutron-counting response.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the thermodynamic temperature of the neutron detector
assembly or neutron-conversion material, characterizing its thermal state
rather than the detector's electrical response or neutron-counting behavior.

The temperature is defined thermodynamically by

$$
\frac{1}{T}=\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial U}\right)_{V,N}
$$

where $T$ is thermodynamic temperature, $S$ is entropy, $U$ is internal
energy, $V$ is volume, and $N$ is the amount of material or particle number
held fixed in the derivative. The quantity applies to the specified detector
or converter material and is distinct from the local material temperature at
a sensor attachment point. It is not the neutron-energy threshold
represented by energy of a neutron detector.

items.name: lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron lithium source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected lithium atom
contributing three equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The lithium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral lithium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. It is the lithium-specific component of the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection),
rather than the raw lithium-atom delivery rate.

For lithium, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium equivalent-electron source
rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the raw lithium atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}=3$ is lithium's dimensionless atomic
number.

The equivalent-electron convention assigns three source counts to each
injected lithium atom and excludes other gas species. This rate is the time
derivative of the corresponding accumulated lithium count; its atomic-number
weighting distinguishes it from the [helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

Sign convention: Positive when lithium is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: alpha_angle_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Signed inclination of the first axis of an oblique parallelogram
cross-section of an axisymmetric ferritic element, measured
counter-clockwise from the outward radial direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the alpha orientation of the first axis of an oblique,
parallelogram-shaped cross-section belonging to a single axisymmetric
ferritic element. It specifies the primary orientation of that element in
the poloidal plane.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the signed inclination
is defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}(\mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}},\, \mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}})
$$

where $\alpha$ is the alpha inclination angle, $\mathbf{a}_1$ is the
oriented unit vector along the first axis of the parallelogram
cross-section, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the outward radial unit vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector, and $\operatorname{atan2}$
is the signed two-argument arctangent.

The quantity applies to one ferritic element and is not an aggregate over
multiple elements. It describes the first axis only; it is distinct from the
[tilt angle of the ferritic element](name:tilt_angle_of_ferritic_element),
which describes the inclination of the second side. Together, the alpha and
tilt angles specify the orientations of the two oblique sides of the
parallelogram cross-section.

The same alpha-orientation concept is used for other oblique component
cross-sections, including an [alpha angle of an iron core
segment](name:alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment).

Sign convention: Positive when the first axis tilts from the outward radial
direction toward increasing $Z$, counter-clockwise in the poloidal $(R,Z)$
plane.

items.name: absorbed_radiated_power_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Net photon power deposited on one divertor target surface after subtracting
radiative power reflected from that surface.
items.documentation:
Absorbed radiated power at a divertor target is the net photon-energy rate
deposited on one specified target surface. It includes incident radiative
energy absorbed by the target and excludes the reflected portion.

The net absorbed radiative power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}} = P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}} - P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{abs,rad}}$ is the absorbed radiated power,
$P_{\mathrm{inc,rad}}$ is the incident radiative power reaching the target,
and $P_{\mathrm{ref,rad}}$ is the radiative power reflected from the target.

This quantity applies to one divertor target and excludes conductive,
convective, charged-particle, and other nonradiative deposition channels.
Summation over all divertor targets gives power of the divertor due to
radiation; the broader radiative deposition concept is described by power
due to radiation.

items.name: vertical_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective convection coefficient relating convective flux of vertical
momentum to its density for one neutral species in one resolved internal
state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed effective coefficient governing convective
transport of the vertical component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by
one neutral species in one specified internal state in edge plasma. Vertical
is the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The convective closure for the selected vertical momentum component is:

$$
\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_{0a,Z}
$$

where $\Pi_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of vertical
momentum across a surface along its chosen normal,
$V_{0a,Z}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this convection coefficient, and $g_{0a,Z}$ is
the vertical momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes the selected
neutral species, and $a$ identifies its resolved internal state.

No sum over neutral species or internal states is implied. The vertical
label identifies the transported momentum component; the surface-normal
transport direction need not be vertical. This effective transport
coefficient is distinct from the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Its convective flux
contribution excludes gradient-driven transport represented by [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), as well as local momentum sources.

The [toroidal neutral-state momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity) is the
corresponding coefficient for transport of toroidal rather than vertical
momentum.

Sign convention: Positive when the convective flux of momentum directed
along increasing $Z$ crosses the surface along its chosen normal.

items.name: length_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Total physical arclength of the optical fiber centerline in a fiber-optic
current sensor, defining its optical propagation distance and distributed
magneto-optic interaction length.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total arclength of the optical fiber centerline forming
the fiber-optic current sensor. It includes the complete winding path and is
not the straight-line distance between endpoints or the length of the sensor
outline.

For a centerline parameterized by an arbitrary parameter $u$, the fiber
length is defined by

$$
L = \int_{u_0}^{u_1} \left|\frac{d\mathbf{r}}{du}\right|\,du
$$

where $L$ is the total fiber arclength, $\mathbf{r}(u)$ is the centerline
position, and $u_0$ and $u_1$ delimit the fiber path. The length sets the
optical propagation distance; accumulated Faraday rotation additionally
depends on the magnetic-field projection along the winding and the [Verdet
constant](name:verdet_constant_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor).

items.name: y_coordinate_of_divertor_target
items.description:
Signed Cartesian y-coordinate locating the geometric center of the divertor
target surface in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame; positive
values lie along the +y axis.
items.documentation:
Signed Cartesian $y$-coordinate locating the geometric center of the
divertor target surface is the component of that center-point position
vector along $\hat{y}$ in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame with
basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$. Here $x$, $y$, and $z$ are Cartesian
position coordinates, $\hat{z}$ is vertical, and $\hat{x}$ is the horizontal
direction corresponding to zero toroidal angle.

The coordinate is related to the same point's position in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame by

$$
y = R\sin\phi
$$

where $y$ is the signed Cartesian coordinate defined here, $R$ is the major
radius of the target-surface center measured from the toroidal symmetry
axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of that same point, and $Z$ is vertical
height in the cylindrical frame.

The scope is the geometric center point of the divertor target surface. It
is a point coordinate of that surface center, not a coordinate field over
the full target surface, a local surface-tangent coordinate, a cylindrical
coordinate, or an area average over target-surface elements.

Together with
[x_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:x_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and
[z_coordinate_of_divertor_target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target),
this quantity forms the Cartesian position vector of the same center point.
The cylindrical relation implies that the possible value is set by that
point's own $R$ through $|y|\le R$, rather than by a generic device major
radius.

Sign convention: Positive when the divertor target surface center is
displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian
$(x,y,z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$.

items.name: thermal_electron_density
items.description:
Number density of thermal electrons is the local concentration of free
electrons in the bulk thermal population, excluding fast and other
nonthermal electrons. It is a population component of total electron
density, not a fraction.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

Total density is the sum of the thermal and fast populations of the species;
thermal excludes the suprathermal particles that fast names.

The local thermal-electron density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of
the thermal-electron distribution:

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \int f_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-electron number density,
$f_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the distribution of thermal electrons in position and
velocity space, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$
is electron velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
integral covers the thermal component, not the separate fast-electron
population.

This quantity applies to the local bulk thermal-electron population in the
core, edge, and scrape-off layer. Fast, suprathermal, and other nonthermal
electrons are excluded, as are electrons bound in atoms or molecules. The
density is defined locally; any spatial average is an average of this local
quantity rather than part of its population definition.

It is the thermal-population component of [electron
density](name:electron_density), distinct from [fast electron
density](name:fast_electron_density). When thermal and fast electrons form a
complete, nonoverlapping partition, [total electron
density](name:total_electron_density) is the sum of this thermal component
and the fast component.

items.name: upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Upper triangularity of the plasma boundary is the inward major-radius
displacement of its upper vertical extremum from the geometric axis, divided
by the boundary minor radius.
items.documentation:
Triangularity of plasma boundary

Triangularity without a qualifier is the mean of the upper and lower
triangularities; upper and lower triangularity each use one extremum of the
cross-section.

The upper and lower triangularities and their mean are defined by:

$$\delta_{\mathrm{u,l}} = (R_{\mathrm{geo}} - R_{\mathrm{u,l}})/a,\quad \delta = (\delta_{\mathrm{u}} + \delta_{\mathrm{l}})/2$$

where $\delta_{\mathrm{u}}$ is upper triangularity, $\delta_{\mathrm{l}}$ is
[lower triangularity of the plasma
boundary](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), and $\delta$ is
[mean triangularity of the plasma
boundary](name:triangularity_of_plasma_boundary). Here $R_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is
the [major-radius coordinate of the geometric
axis](name:radial_coordinate_of_geometric_axis), $R_{\mathrm{u,l}}$ denotes
the major-radius coordinate of the upper or lower vertical extremum,
respectively, and $a$ is the boundary minor radius, equal to its horizontal
half-width. These coordinates use the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

This quantity describes only the upper extremum of the plasma-boundary
cross-section; it is not an average over both extrema or over nested flux
surfaces. Unlike [upper triangularity of a flux
surface](name:upper_triangularity_of_flux_surface), its locus is restricted
to the plasma boundary. The upper and lower triangularities contribute
equally to the mean boundary triangularity and need not coincide.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Toroidal (φ) component of the gage-dependent vacuum magnetic vector
potential produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component $A_\u03c6$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is
the projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the toroidal direction
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It
represents the toroidally directed external-source contribution produced
solely by toroidal-field coil currents, excluding the contribution generated
by plasma currents.

The component is defined by

$$
A_\phi = \mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $A_\phi$ is the toroidal component, $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the
vacuum magnetic vector potential, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This scalar is the signed toroidal projection of the gage-dependent [vacuum
magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), not its
magnitude or full vector. Together with the [radial vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) and [vertical
vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), it provides the
component decomposition of the vacuum vector potential; plasma-current
contributions remain excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when $A_\phi$ points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description:
Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or
corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by
the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium field. It excludes
externally imposed vacuum perturbations when those are represented
separately.
items.documentation:
Perturbed plasma magnetic field is the complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or
corresponding real perturbation, of the magnetic-field deviation carried by
the confined-plasma response about an equilibrium magnetic field. It
represents magnetic-field bending and current perturbations inside the
confined plasma and excludes any externally imposed vacuum perturbation that
is retained as a separate field.

The plasma-response perturbation is defined by subtracting the equilibrium
field and any separately represented vacuum perturbation from the total
field in the confined plasma region:

$$
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathbf{x},t) = \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x},t) - \mathbf{B}_0(\mathbf{x}) - \delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ is this quantity, $\mathbf{x}$ is
position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic field,
$\mathbf{B}_0$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the externally imposed vacuum magnetic
perturbation that would exist without plasma response. If no separate vacuum
perturbation is present or retained, set $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}=0$;
the field satisfies $\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}=0$.

Externally imposed vacuum-field quantities, including
[perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field),
[radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field),
and non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field_at_control_surface, can drive the plasma
response but are not included in $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$ when
represented separately. Fourier harmonic amplitudes, eigenfunction
components, and spatial projections must carry their stated phase, harmonic,
and direction definitions; they are not interchangeable with the
unrestricted vector. The related component quantities
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
and
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field)
describe resolved quantities: radial is the $\hat{R}$ projection in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, poloidal requires an explicitly
defined poloidal projection direction such as the tangent to increasing
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, and the toroidal entry
denotes the single-harmonic $\hat{\phi}$-resolved quantity specified by that
standard name.

Sign convention: Positive when a real resolved component of
$\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{pl}$, or the real part of a complex resolved
component after applying its stated phase convention, is directed along the
positive basis direction; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame
with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, $+\hat{R}$ is toward increasing
major radius $R$, $+\hat{\phi}$ is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $+\hat{Z}$ is
toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: ammonia_deuterated_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous molecular injection rate of deuterated ammonia (ND3) supplied
to the plasma vessel by gas injection.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the rate at which deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules are
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts ND3 molecules
directly rather than converting them to an equivalent-electron inventory.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of injected ND3
molecules and $t$ is time. The rate is distinct from the [ammonia source
rate](name:ammonia_source_rate), which refers to NH3 molecules, and its time
integral gives the injected molecular inventory represented by the
[accumulated deuterated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count).

items.name: effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description:
Effective vector velocity for convective transport of neutral particles in a
specified internal quantum state, without selecting a particular spatial
component.
items.documentation:
The effective neutral internal-state convection velocity is the vector that
represents particle transport caused by convection for one specified
internal quantum state. It is an advective transport velocity, distinct from
the bulk translational velocity of that state,
[neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity).

The effective velocity is defined from the convective particle flux:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{conv}} = n\,\boldsymbol{v}_{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective particle-flux
vector, $n$ is the number density of neutral particles in the specified
state, and $\boldsymbol{v}_{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective velocity.

The vector includes all spatial components. Its radial component is
represented by
[radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection](name:radial_effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection);
this quantity concerns particle convection rather than velocity associated
specifically with convective momentum transport, represented by
[neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection).
Components are interpreted in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

Sign convention: Positive when each component points along its positive
direction: $+\hat{R}$, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, or
$+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Flux-surface average of the local magnetic-field strength, retaining the
pointwise modulus before averaging over each magnetic surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the magnitude of the total
equilibrium magnetic-field vector. It represents the mean field strength on
a magnetic surface, rather than a component or a vector average.

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\left\langle \lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert \right\rangle_{\psi} = \frac{\oint_{\psi} \lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert\,\mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}{\oint_{\psi} \mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the total equilibrium magnetic-field vector, $\psi$ is
the scalar label of the magnetic flux surface, $\mathrm{d}S$ is the
surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of that
surface label. The aggregation is the normalized surface integral with
weighting $\mathrm{d}S/\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert$.

The quantity applies to all components of the equilibrium field on the
selected magnetic flux surface and is non-negative. It excludes any signed
field component, any species or source decomposition, and the magnitude of a
vector obtained by averaging $\mathbf{B}$ before taking its modulus.

It is the flux-surface-averaged transformation of [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude). It differs from
[flux-surface-averaged square of magnetic-field
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude),
which averages the squared field strength rather than the field strength
itself.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the measurement position, specifying signed height
relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the measurement position specifies its signed height
along the symmetry-axis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $Z$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector
from the coordinate origin to the measurement position, and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis in the
positive vertical direction. The other frame coordinates are $R$, the major
radius, and $\phi$, the toroidal angle.

This quantity applies to the specified measurement position without an
implied spatial average. It is a geometric coordinate, not a measured field
value or a vertical extent. The [vertical coordinate of a line-of-sight
reference point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_line_of_sight) uses the same
projection for that distinct locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the coordinate origin
to the measurement position has a positive projection along the positive
vertical direction.

items.name: neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Vector diffusion coefficient governing diffusive transport of momentum in
the neutral particle population, with directional components representing
anisotropic momentum diffusivities along the radial, poloidal, and toroidal
directions.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum diffusion coefficient quantifies the effective
diffusivity that drives collisional and turbulent spreading of
neutral-particle momentum down local velocity gradients. As a vector
quantity, its components represent the diagonal entries of the momentum
diffusion tensor for neutrals in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, capturing anisotropy across the radial, poloidal, and toroidal
directions independently.

The diffusive neutral momentum flux density along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is
governed by:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{diff},i} = -\rho_n \, D_{\mathrm{mom},i} \, \frac{\partial u_{n,i}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\rho_n$ is the neutral mass density, $u_{n,i}$ is the neutral flow
velocity component along $\hat{e}_i$, and $D_{\mathrm{mom},i}$ is the
corresponding directional component of this coefficient.

In edge plasma modeling, the dominant physical mechanisms determining this
diffusivity are charge-exchange with background ions, neutral-neutral
collisions, and elastic scattering; the resulting coefficient is strongly
anisotropic in realistic magnetic geometries. The
radial_neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient gives the cross-field
component driving transport across magnetic flux surfaces. For comparison,
the analogous momentum diffusivity for the bulk plasma is captured by
plasma_momentum_diffusivity, and the toroidal ion channel counterpart is
described by toroidal_momentum_diffusivity.

items.name: turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Signed number of complete winding turns in a toroidal magnetic-field probe
coil, with orientation referenced to the positive toroidal direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed number of complete winding turns in a toroidal
magnetic-field probe coil. It represents the coil's oriented electromagnetic
coupling to the toroidal magnetic-field component, rather than a
magnetic-field value.

The scope is one toroidal magnetic-field probe coil. The count refers to its
physical complete windings, includes their common orientation, and does not
aggregate turns over multiple probes or channels. It excludes the coil's
enclosed area, length, induced voltage, and any calibration factor.

Reversing the winding orientation reverses the sign. Together with the [area
of the toroidal magnetic-field
probe](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), this count sets the
ideal flux-linkage sensitivity to the toroidal magnetic field. It is the
literal winding-count specialization related to the [effective turn count of
a passive loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), which can
represent equivalent or homogenized windings and may therefore differ from a
complete-turn count. The corresponding poloidal-orientation quantity is the
[turn count of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

The orientation is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Value of the radius-like toroidal-flux label on the magnetic surface passing
through the magnetic axis; it is zero because enclosed toroidal flux
vanishes there.
items.documentation:
The toroidal flux coordinate at the magnetic axis is the value of the
radius-like flux-surface label on the magnetic-axis reference surface. It
identifies the origin of the toroidal-flux radial coordinate and is not a
geometric distance from the machine symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the magnetic
surface, and $B_0$ is the positive reference vacuum toroidal magnetic-field
strength. At the magnetic axis, the enclosed toroidal flux is zero, so this
value is zero.

The quantity applies to the single magnetic-axis locus and is neither a
flux-surface average nor an integral over a finite region. It is the axis
value of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate), not the coordinate of an
arbitrary flux surface or a geometric major- or minor-radius measurement.

The [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) supplies the
enclosed-flux quantity in the defining relation, while the corresponding
normalized toroidal-flux coordinate uses axis and boundary values to form a
dimensionless radial label.

items.name: fast_electron_pressure
items.description:
Kinetic pressure associated with the fast electron population, retaining
directional momentum transport rather than imposing an isotropic thermal
approximation.
items.documentation:
Fast electron pressure is the kinetic pressure-tensor contribution of the
suprathermal electron population, representing random electron momentum
transport carried by fast electrons.

For the fast-electron distribution function, its defining relation is

$$
\mathbf{P}_{e,f}=m_e\int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,f})(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{e,f})f_{e,f}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{e,f}$ is the fast-electron pressure tensor, $m_e$ is
electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{e,f}$ is the
mean velocity of the fast-electron population, $f_{e,f}(\mathbf{v})$ is its
velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

The scope is the aggregate suprathermal electron population, including its
directional pressure response and excluding the bulk thermal-electron
contribution. It is not restricted to a single magnetic-field direction or
to an isotropic stress representation.

The directional projections of this quantity are represented by [parallel
fast electron pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure) and
[perpendicular fast electron
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure). Within the broader
[electron pressure](name:electron_pressure) concept, it supplies the
fast-population contribution; [total electron
pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) combines fast and thermal electron
contributions in the complete electron population.

Sign convention: Positive when the relevant pressure-tensor projection is
compressive rather than tensile.

items.name: ion_charge_state_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description:
Wave power absorbed by ions of a specified charge state from a single
coherent beam-tracing beam, giving the charge-state-resolved ion
contribution to total path-integrated wave energy deposition for that beam.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state absorbed power of a beam-tracing beam is the total wave
power transferred from a single traced coherent electromagnetic beam to the
ionic population in a specified charge state over its computed propagation
path. It is the charge-state-resolved ion contribution to the species-summed
[absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam),
complementing the electron channel provided by
[electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:electron_absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam).

For a ray arc length $s$ increasing along the direction of wave propagation,
the absorbed power for ion charge state $z$ is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},z} = \int_{s_0}^{s_{\mathrm{end}}} 2\kappa_{i,z}(s)\,P(s)\,ds
$$

where $\kappa_{i,z}(s)$ is the spatial amplitude-damping coefficient for the
specified ion charge state in m$^{-1}$, $P(s)$ is the remaining beam power
in W at arc-length position $s$ in m, and $s_0$ and $s_{\mathrm{end}}$ are
the start and end arc-length positions. The factor of 2 converts
amplitude-damping to power-damping because wave power is proportional to
squared wave-field amplitude, consistent with the parent formulation.

Summing over all charge states of all ion species and adding the electron
contribution recovers
[absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam](name:absorbed_power_of_beam_tracing_beam)
for that beam. The residual power_of_beam_tracing_beam at the beam end
equals the entering power minus the sum of all species- and
charge-state-resolved absorbed powers.

items.name: inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the Luce shape coefficient for
the high-field-side corner pair, referenced to an ellipse defined by
boundary size and shaping.
items.documentation:
Inner squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape
coefficient characterizing how the high-field-side corners of the last
closed flux surface depart from a reference ellipse. It covers the inner
corner behavior represented separately by the [upper-inner
squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower-inner
squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary) quantities,
rather than selecting one vertical quadrant.

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coefficient for an inner
quadrant is

$$
\zeta = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $O$ is the reference-ellipse center, $D$ is the boundary intersection
along the corner diagonal, $E$ is the corresponding ellipse intersection,
and $F$ is the corner of the circumscribing rectangle; the overbars denote
distances. The reference ellipse is set by the boundary minor radius,
elongation, and triangularity. This component refines the whole-boundary
[squareness of the plasma boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) to
its high-field-side corners.

items.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
items.description:
Temperature of bulk electrons from random translational motion,
volume-averaged inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, including
during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
Temperature of bulk electrons averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by
the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of their local
energy-equivalent kinetic temperature. For nonrelativistic electrons, the
local temperature equals two-thirds of the mean random kinetic energy per
particle, excluding directed mean-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature,
$T_e$ is the local bulk electron temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the
differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies throughout that enclosed volume, including during
plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial
volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a local value. It
differs from [line-averaged electron
temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along
a plasma chord. It is neither total electron thermal energy nor a radiation
brightness temperature.

This quantity is obtained by applying volume averaging to [electron
temperature](name:electron_temperature); [volume-averaged ion
temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the corresponding
spatial average to a specified ion species. It supplies the denominator of
the [ratio of magnetic-axis to volume-averaged electron
temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature),
which expresses central electron-temperature peaking relative to the
plasma-wide mean.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective kinematic coefficient for field-aligned diffusion of an ion
species’ momentum, driven by gradients of its charge-state-averaged parallel
flow velocity.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion momentum diffusivity is the effective kinematic coefficient
governing field-aligned diffusive transport of the parallel component of
[momentum](name:momentum) for a specified ion species. It is the
field-aligned ion specialization of [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity).

In a local kinematic diffusion closure, the field-aligned diffusive flux of
parallel ion momentum is:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_i n_i D_{i,\parallel}\frac{\partial v_{i,\parallel}}{\partial \ell_\parallel}
$$

where $i$ labels the ion species, $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
flux of parallel momentum along the magnetic field, $m_i$ is the ion mass,
$n_i$ is the species number density summed over all ionic charge states,
$D_{i,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the
density-weighted mean parallel flow velocity over all ionic charge states,
and $\ell_\parallel$ is arc length increasing along the local magnetic-field
direction. For nonnegative diffusivity, the flux opposes the parallel
velocity gradient.

The coefficient applies to the collective momentum of one ion species,
excluding neutral particles and other ion species. It belongs to the
collective-flow closure and is not a sum of charge-state diffusivities; the
[charge-state-resolved parallel momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead applies to one specified charge state.

This closure acts on the parallel flow-velocity gradient rather than
directly on the momentum-density gradient. It excludes convective momentum
transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources. Unlike the
[parallel ion momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), it describes spatial
diffusive redistribution rather than local momentum relaxation.

items.name: ion_state_source_rate
items.description:
Ion charge-state source rate is the net volumetric rate of particle addition
or removal for one specified charge state of an ion species.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state source rate is the net volumetric rate at which particles
enter or leave a specified charge state of an ion species. It supplies the
particle-number source term in that charge state's density transport
equation.

The source enters the particle continuity equation as

$$
\frac{\partial n_q}{\partial t}+\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q=S_q
$$

where $q$ is the specified ion charge number, $n_q$ is the number density of
that charge state, $t$ is time, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_q$ is its
particle-number flux density, $S_q$ is its net volumetric particle source
rate, and $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial divergence.

This quantity is resolved by ion species and charge state, not summed over
charge states. Positive values indicate net particle gain and negative
values indicate net particle loss for the specified state. Transfers between
charge states contribute even when they leave the species' total particle
number unchanged. The quantity counts particles rather than electric charge;
spatial transport is represented separately by the flux-divergence term.

Integrating this volumetric source over the volume enclosed by a magnetic
flux surface gives the [cumulative ion charge-state source rate inside that
surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate),
rather than another volumetric source rate.

items.name: thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net rate per
volume at which particles enter or leave the thermal population.
items.documentation:
Thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at
which particles enter or leave the thermal population of a specified
species. It is the source term for thermal particle-number density,
aggregated over orbit classes.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_n^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{th}}-S_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_n^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal particle source rate,
$S_{n,\mathrm{in}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local volumetric rate of addition
to the thermal population, $S_{n,\mathrm{out}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local
volumetric rate of removal from it, $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface
label, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity combines the included particle source and sink processes for
the specified species; it is neither summed over different species nor
integrated over the enclosed volume. Positive values indicate net addition
and negative values net removal. Thermalization of nonthermal particles can
contribute positively, while acceleration out of the thermal population can
contribute negatively, but the quantity is not restricted to thermalization.
It excludes changes confined to the nonthermal population and is distinct
from the full thermal-density time derivative, which also includes spatial
transport.

Its orbit-resolved decomposition is the sum of the [co-passing thermal
particle source rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate),
[counter-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), and [trapped
thermal particle source rate](name:trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate).
Transfers between these thermal orbit classes cancel in the aggregate and do
not alone change the total thermal particle number.

items.name: tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron tritium source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, with each injected tritium atom contributing
one equivalent-electron count.
items.documentation:
The tritium source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral tritium with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{T}} = 1$ is
admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count rate. It is the tritium-specific component of the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}} = Z_{\mathrm{T}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}} = \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the raw tritium atom delivery rate in atoms per
second, and $Z_{\mathrm{T}}$ is tritium's atomic number. The rate is the
instantaneous derivative of the accumulated inventory [accumulated tritium
count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection), and it
counts delivered atoms rather than plasma electron content or ionization
state.

Sign convention: Positive when tritium gas is being delivered into the
vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: voltage_of_flux_loop
items.description:
Terminal voltage of a flux loop is the signed, unintegrated electrical
potential difference at the loop terminals. It is induced by the time
variation of the oriented magnetic flux linked by the loop and is related to
that flux by Faraday's law.
items.documentation:
Terminal voltage of a flux loop is the signed, unintegrated electrical
potential difference between the designated terminals of a flux loop. It
represents the electromotive response of the loop to variation of the
oriented magnetic flux linked by its conducting contour.

The defining relation to the loop flux is Faraday's law for the oriented
loop contour:

$$
V_\mathrm{loop}(t) = -\frac{d\Phi_\mathrm{loop}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{loop}$ is the terminal voltage of the flux loop, $t$ is
time, and $\Phi_\mathrm{loop}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux of the flux
loop](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_of_flux_loop) associated with the oriented
surface bounded by the loop; the contour orientation and surface normal are
related by the right-hand rule.

The quantity applies to an individual flux loop and to the terminal pair
with its specified polarity; it is not aggregated over multiple flux loops.
It is the raw terminal voltage, not the time-integrated flux, not the loop's
[area](name:area_of_flux_loop), and not an equilibrium-reconstructed
magnetic flux.

Time integration gives the linked flux up to an integration constant:
$\Phi_\mathrm{loop}(t)-\Phi_\mathrm{loop}(t_0) = -\int_{t_0}^{t}
V_\mathrm{loop}(t')\,dt'$, where $t_0$ is a reference time and $t'$ is the
integration time variable. The [area of the flux
loop](name:area_of_flux_loop) defines the geometric aperture entering the
flux linkage but is not itself part of the terminal-voltage quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the oriented magnetic flux linked by the loop
decreases with time for the specified terminal polarity and loop
orientation.

items.name: radial_effective_neutral_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective neutral-particle diffusivity relating diffusive flux to the
neutral number-density gradient along R in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the effective Fickian diffusivity governing neutral-particle
diffusion along the cylindrical radial direction. It is the radial component
of [effective neutral diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_diffusivity),
rather than an aggregate over transport directions.

The radial diffusive flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{n,R}^{\mathrm{eff}}\frac{\partial n_n}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the neutral-particle diffusive flux
in the radial direction, $D_{n,R}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective radial
diffusivity, $n_n$ is neutral-particle number density, and $R$ is major
radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The negative
sign specifies diffusion down the neutral-density gradient. The coefficient
applies to the diffusive contribution of the neutral density transport
equation; advective transport and particle source or sink terms are distinct
contributions.

items.name: launched_power_of_electron_cyclotron_beam
items.description:
Power injected into the vacuum vessel by one electron-cyclotron beam after
transmission losses and before plasma absorption or reflection.
items.documentation:
Launched power is the electromagnetic power carried by one specified
electron-cyclotron beam into the vacuum vessel toward the plasma. It
represents injected beam power rather than energy deposited in the plasma.

The power is defined as the rate of electromagnetic energy transport:

$$
P_{\mathrm{launched}} = \frac{dE}{dt}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{launched}}$ is the launched beam power, $E$ is the
electromagnetic energy transported by the beam, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to an individual electron-cyclotron beam and is not an
aggregate over multiple beams or a complete launcher system. Transmission
losses before launch are excluded from the launched value; plasma absorption
and power reflected after launch are also excluded.

The beam's carrier frequency, represented by the [electron-cyclotron beam
frequency](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam), determines its
cyclotron-resonance condition, while launched power specifies the strength
of the injected electromagnetic beam.

items.name: inner_radius_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Inner radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the inner
circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a
current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the boundary between the hollow
central region and the conducting annular region.
items.documentation:
Inner radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the inner
circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a
current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the boundary between the hollow
central region and the conducting annular region.

For the inner circular boundary in the poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the inner radius
