$a_\mathrm{inner}$ is the distance from the filament cross-section center
$(R_c, Z_c)$ to any point $(R, Z)$ on that boundary:

$$
a_\mathrm{inner} = \sqrt{(R - R_c)^2 + (Z - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $(R_c, Z_c)$ is the
center of the annular cross-section, and $(R, Z)$ is a point on the inner
circular boundary.

This quantity applies to the hollow-disk annular representation of a
discrete plasma current-carrying filament and denotes the smaller of its two
concentric boundary radii. The current-carrying cross-section occupies the
region outside $a_\mathrm{inner}$ and inside $a_\mathrm{outer}$, where
$a_\mathrm{outer}$ is the [outer radius of the plasma
filament](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament), with $0 \le
a_\mathrm{inner} \le a_\mathrm{outer}$.

Together with the [outer radius of the plasma
filament](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament), this quantity determines
the width of the plasma filament as the radial thickness of the annulus and
the area of the plasma filament as the area of the current-carrying annular
region. It excludes the outer boundary radius itself, the annular width or
area, the [height of the plasma filament](name:height_of_plasma_filament),
the curvature radius of a noncircular contour segment, and the major radius
of a filament centerline about the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: krypton_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Krypton ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all krypton ionization states.
items.documentation:
Krypton density at a limiter is the local number density of krypton ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance at the plasma–limiter contact, where open scrape-off-layer field
lines terminate on the material boundary.

Unless a single charge state is explicitly specified, the quantity
represents the charge-state-summed total:

$$
n_\mathrm{Kr} = \sum_{q=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the number density of krypton ions in
ionization state $q$, ranging from $q = 1$ (singly ionized) to $q = 36$
(fully stripped). Neutral krypton atoms are excluded from this quantity.

Krypton is a high-$Z$ noble gas ($Z = 36$) injected as a seeding impurity to
enhance radiative dissipation in the scrape-off layer, redistributing heat
load away from plasma-facing components. Its local density at the limiter
characterizes krypton availability for charge exchange, ionization, and
plasma–material interactions at the wall. Even modest krypton concentrations
significantly elevate
[effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter) due to its
high nuclear charge.

Within the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) family, krypton
density serves as a heavier-impurity counterpart to lighter noble-gas seeds
such as [argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), and
contrasts with fuel-ion species such as
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). Under
quasi-neutrality, the charge-weighted sum of all ion densities at the
limiter equals
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter).

items.name: perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part
items.description:
Real part of the complex first-order plasma pressure perturbation
eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability
analysis.
items.documentation:
The real part of the complex pressure perturbation eigenfunction $\tilde{p}$
gives the in-phase component of the linearized first-order pressure
variation associated with a given toroidal MHD mode, distributed over the
poloidal cross-section.

The full pressure field decomposes as:

$$
p = p_0 + \text{Re}\!\left[\tilde{p}(R,Z)\, e^{i(n_\phi \phi - \omega t)}\right]
$$

where $p_0$ is the equilibrium pressure profile, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal
mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $\omega$ is the complex MHD eigenfrequency. The
quantity $\text{Re}(\tilde{p})$ is the real component of the parent
eigenfunction perturbed_plasma_pressure evaluated on the poloidal plane.

Together with the
[perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part),
it fully specifies the complex amplitude and phase of $\tilde{p}$; the
amplitude is $|\tilde{p}| = \sqrt{\text{Re}(\tilde{p})^2 +
\text{Im}(\tilde{p})^2}$. Analogous real-part eigenfunctions for other
linearized MHD perturbation quantities include
[perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part)
and
[perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part).

This quantity is produced by linear MHD stability solvers as part of the
eigenvalue problem on the poloidal grid. Because the eigenfunction phase is
fixed by the solver normalization convention, the absolute sign of
$\text{Re}(\tilde{p})$ is convention-dependent; only relative magnitudes and
phase angles among the perturbed quantities in the same eigenfunction carry
physical content.

items.name: lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Lower thickness of a breeder blanket module is the non-negative geometric
separation through the lower cap, measured normal to its exterior boundary
and main-body interface.
items.documentation:
Lower thickness of a breeder blanket module is the geometric thickness of
the cap that closes the module at its lower end. The reference surfaces are
the lower exterior boundary of the cap and the interface where the lower cap
joins the main module body. It is distinct from the overall thickness of a
breeder blanket module and the corresponding [upper thickness of a breeder
blanket module](name:upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module).

The lower-cap thickness is the normal projection of the separation between
the reference surfaces:

$$
t_{\mathrm{lower}} = \left|\left(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ext}} - \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{int}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\right|
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{int}}$ are
corresponding points on the lower exterior boundary and cap-to-body
interface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the local unit normal directed through the
cap, and $t_{\mathrm{lower}}$ is the lower-cap thickness. The quantity is a
non-negative geometric magnitude; it is not a signed vertical coordinate or
displacement and excludes the thicknesses of internal breeder, coolant, or
shielding layers.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged electron number density at the plasma boundary, using
inverse-magnitude poloidal-flux-gradient weighting rather than a pointwise
value.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle = \oint n_e\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_e\rangle$ is the averaged electron number density, $n_e$ is
the local electron number density, the subscript $e$ identifies electrons,
$S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, $\psi$
is poloidal magnetic flux, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

This quantity applies only to the electron population at the plasma
boundary. Its aggregation is over the flux surface with inverse-gradient
weighting, not over particle species; it is neither an ion density, a
pointwise density, a volume average, nor an unweighted surface average.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [electron number density at the
plasma boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary): the parent
quantity supplies $n_e$ at each surface point, while this quantity applies
the normalized flux-surface integral. It differs from [flux-surface-averaged
total ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary),
which represents charged ions rather than electrons.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Nonnegative factor scaling the collisionless free-streaming cap on the flux
of magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by a specified ion charge state
in edge-plasma transport.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on transport
of the magnetic-field-parallel component of [momentum](name:momentum)
carried by one specified ion charge state in an edge-plasma fluid closure.
Parallel identifies the transported momentum component, not necessarily the
direction in which that momentum crosses a surface.

The coefficient enters the flux bound as:

$$
\left|\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}(\hat{n})\right| \leq \alpha_{s,\parallel}\,\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}(\hat{n})
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\parallel$ denotes
the local magnetic-field direction, $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the
transport surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited flux of
parallel momentum through that surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is
the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude, and
$\alpha_{s,\parallel}$ is this limiter coefficient. The reference magnitude
and the detailed limiting function are closure-dependent.

The coefficient is nonnegative and charge-state resolved; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states. It scales the flux-magnitude bound
without reversing the underlying flux direction and is distinct from a
momentum diffusivity or damping rate.

It specializes the [ion charge-state momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) to
magnetic-field-parallel momentum. The [diamagnetic momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) instead
limits transport of the diamagnetic momentum contribution.

items.name: ion_torque_density
items.description:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for all ion species and
charge states, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for all ion species and charge states is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to the ion population per unit volume. It
retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a
toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{i}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i}$ is the ion torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{i}$ is the total angular momentum of all ion species and
charge states in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The parent [torque
density](name:torque_density) gives the corresponding general torque-density
concept, while [toroidal ion torque
density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density) is its major-radius-weighted
toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: co_passing_torque_density
items.description:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for the co-passing plasma
population, retaining the complete torque-vector direction and all
applicable transfer mechanisms.
items.documentation:
Torque density for the co-passing plasma population is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to that population per unit volume. It
retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a
toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the angular momentum of the co-passing
population, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The [toroidal co-passing
torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density) is its
major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [toroidal torque
density](name:toroidal_torque_density) selects the corresponding toroidal
component without restricting the orbit class. The [torque
density](name:torque_density) parent provides the common vector quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: plasma_mass_density_real_part
items.description:
Real part of a complex plasma mass-density quantity, representing the
in-phase quadrature relative to the chosen complex phase. It is the real
component only, not the full complex density or its imaginary quadrature.
items.documentation:
Plasma mass density real part is the real-valued quadrature of a complex
plasma mass-density quantity. It represents the component aligned with the
chosen real phase of the complex representation and is not the full complex
quantity.

The decomposition into real and imaginary quadratures is

$$
\tilde{\rho} = \rho_R + i\rho_I,\qquad \rho_R = \operatorname{Re}\{\tilde{\rho}\}
$$

where $\tilde{\rho}$ is the complex plasma mass-density quantity, $\rho_R$
is its real part, and $\rho_I$ is its imaginary part.

This abstraction covers concrete real-part quantities such as the [perturbed
plasma mass density real
part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_real_part). It excludes the
imaginary quadrature, the complex modulus, the phase, and the full complex
field; for linear-mode quantities, multiplication of the complex field by a
constant phase changes the numerical split between $\rho_R$ and $\rho_I$ but
not the represented physical mode.

Sign convention: Positive when the real quadrature represents an in-phase
increase of the local plasma mass density for the chosen complex phase.

items.name: upper_triangularity_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless upper triangularity shape parameter for a nested magnetic flux
surface, given by the normalized inward radial displacement of its upper
vertical extremum.
items.documentation:
Upper triangularity of a flux surface is the dimensionless triangularity
shape parameter defined at the upper vertical extremum of a nested magnetic
flux surface. It is the normalized inward radial displacement of that upper
extremum in a poloidal cross-section.

For the upper vertical extremum, the defining relation is:

$$
\delta_u = \frac{R_{\mathrm{axis}} - R_u}{a}
$$

where $\delta_u$ is upper triangularity, $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the
major-radius coordinate of the magnetic axis, $R_u$ is the major-radius
coordinate of the upper vertical extremum, and $a$ is the minor radius of
the flux surface. These coordinates are defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies separately to each nested magnetic flux surface
identified by its poloidal magnetic-flux label. It represents only the upper
extremum and is not an aggregate over the upper and lower extrema or over
multiple flux surfaces.

It is distinct from [lower triangularity of a flux
surface](name:lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface), which uses the lower
vertical extremum. It also differs from [upper triangularity of the plasma
boundary](name:upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), which applies only
to the outer plasma boundary rather than to an arbitrary nested flux
surface.

Upper triangularity is the upper-extremum branch of [triangularity of a flux
surface](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface), whose definition permits the
relevant upper or lower vertical extremum. The upper and lower quantities
together describe the asymmetric triangular shaping of a flux-surface
cross-section.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless plasma-wide carbon abundance defined as the ratio of
volume-averaged carbon number density to volume-averaged electron number
density. The carbon density is summed over all carbon charge states.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless plasma-wide carbon abundance is the ratio of volume-averaged
carbon number density to volume-averaged electron number density. It
represents the elemental carbon abundance relative to electrons over the
same plasma volume.

The defining ratio is

$$
f_{C,V} = \frac{\langle n_C \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V} = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=0}^{6} n_{\mathrm{C},q} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{C,V}$ is the ratio of volume-averaged carbon density to
volume-averaged electron density, $\langle n_C \rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged carbon density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density),
$\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_C$ is the [carbon
density](name:carbon_density), $n_{\mathrm{C},q}$ is the local number
density of carbon nuclei in charge state $q$, $q$ is the carbon charge-state
index with $q=0$ for neutral carbon and $q=6$ for fully stripped carbon, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the same plasma volume for
numerator and denominator.

The population is elemental carbon in the plasma volume, with the numerator
summed over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states. The aggregation
convention is a ratio of two volume averages using the same volume
weighting; it is not the volume average of the local ratio $n_C/n_e$.

This quantity is not an ion-only carbon abundance, not a fraction of total
particle density, and not a charge-weighted impurity measure. It is the
carbon member of the same volume-averaged impurity-abundance family as the
[boron abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
and it differs from the [ratio of total ion density to electron
density](name:ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density), which
aggregates over all ion species rather than isolating elemental carbon.

items.name: accumulated_lithium_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative post-breakdown lithium inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as three equivalent-electron counts per injected lithium atom.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the cumulative inventory of lithium atoms introduced by gas
injection after plasma breakdown, re-expressed as an equivalent-electron
count. It represents delivered lithium inventory, not the number of
electrons currently present in the plasma or a lithium ion charge-state
population.

The cumulative value at time $t$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{Li}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li,eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron lithium
inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is lithium's atomic number and equals three,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t')$ is the lithium-atom injection rate at
integration time $t'$, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

The accumulation begins at plasma breakdown and includes only lithium
delivered by gas injection, with three equivalent-electron counts assigned
to each lithium atom. It excludes lithium introduced during prefill,
represented by [accumulated lithium prefill count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection), and
excludes inventories of other species. The equivalent-electron weighting is
an inventory convention, not a measurement of lithium ionization or the
instantaneous plasma electron population.

The corresponding instantaneous source is the [lithium source rate due to
gas injection](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection); integrating
that source from breakdown gives the accumulated post-breakdown inventory.

items.name: neutral_species_energy_flux
items.description:
Neutral species energy flux is the signed neutral-species
energy-flux-density vector; its projection normal to an oriented surface
gives the crossing power per unit area for one specified neutral species,
summed over all internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral species energy flux is the signed energy-flux-density vector carried
by one specified neutral atom or molecule species. Its projection onto an
oriented surface normal gives the rate at which energy carried by that
neutral species crosses the surface per unit area, summed over all internal
states of the species and including convective and conductive contributions
when those channels are in scope.

For an oriented surface with unit normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, the signed
surface-normal flux associated with the neutral-species energy flux
$\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is defined by

$$
F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})} = \mathbf{q}_{E,N_s} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $N_s$ labels the selected neutral species, the subscript $E$ denotes
energy transport, $\mathbf{q}_{E,N_s}$ is the neutral-species
energy-flux-density vector, $F_{E,N_s}^{(\hat{\mathbf{n}})}$ is its signed
surface-normal projection, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ defines the positive
crossing direction.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral species in the neutral
population and is aggregated by summing contributions from all internal
states of that species. It is species-resolved: it is not the all-neutral
[neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux), not total plasma energy
flux, not an electromagnetic Poynting flux, and not [electron energy
flux](name:electron_energy_flux) or [ion energy flux](name:ion_energy_flux).

The vector may be projected onto specified directions to form directional
components. [Poloidal neutral species energy
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_species_energy_flux) is the poloidal directional
component of this neutral-species vector, whereas this parent quantity does
not itself select a poloidal, parallel, or surface-normal projection. When
the same energy channels and internal-state aggregation are used, summing
this species-resolved vector over neutral species gives the all-neutral
[neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-species energy-flux-density
vector has a component in the chosen positive projection direction or chosen
unit normal to an oriented surface.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of oxygen ions flux-surface-averaged at the plasma boundary,
summed over all charged oxygen ionization states and excluding neutral
oxygen.
items.documentation:
Number density of oxygen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{O}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{O}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, /\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{O}}\rangle$ is the averaged oxygen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the local oxygen-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux. The factor $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of the
spatial gradient of poloidal magnetic flux, and both closed integrals extend
over $S$.

This quantity is not a local point value, a volume average, an individual
charge-state density, or a density that includes neutral oxygen. It is the
flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [oxygen density at the plasma
boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary), using
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting to replace the pointwise value with
a surface mean.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_line_of_sight
items.description:
Signed normalized toroidal-flux label at the line-of-sight point closest to
the magnetic axis, positive above and negative below the axis.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal flux label assigned to the point on
a line of sight that approaches the magnetic axis most closely. Its sign
records whether that closest point lies above or below the magnetic axis.

The signed closest-approach value is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{LOS}} = \operatorname{sgn}(Z_* - Z_{\mathrm{axis}})\,\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x}_*),
\qquad
\mathbf{x}_* = \underset{\mathbf{x}\in\mathrm{LOS}}{\operatorname{arg\,min}}\,\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{LOS}}$ is this signed line-of-sight value,
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), $\mathbf{x}$ is a
point on the line of sight, $\mathbf{x}_*$ is the closest-approach point,
and $\mathrm{LOS}$ denotes the line of sight. The function
$\operatorname{sgn}$ supplies the sign of its argument; $Z_*$ is the
vertical coordinate of the closest-approach point and $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is
the vertical coordinate of the magnetic axis. Here $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$ are
the major-radius, toroidal-angle, and vertical coordinates in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The quantity applies to one line of sight and uses only the selected
closest-approach point; it is not a line average, line integral,
flux-surface average, or volume aggregate. Unlike normalized toroidal flux
coordinate of measurement position, it does not describe the coordinate at
an arbitrary single measurement point.

It is obtained from the parent [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) by evaluating that
magnetic-surface label at the closest-approach point and appending the
above/below-axis sign. The underlying unsigned label increases outward from
the magnetic axis toward the equilibrium boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the closest point on the line of sight lies
above the magnetic axis, meaning $Z_* > Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the signed flux through a
horizontal disk centered on the symmetry axis and bounded by a toroidal
circle through a boundary point.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the signed equilibrium flux
through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded
by a toroidal circle through a boundary point. It is a locus-specific
poloidal specialization of [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the boundary
poloidal flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b} = \int_0^{R_b} B_Z(R',Z_b)\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$ is the boundary poloidal magnetic flux, $R_b$
and $Z_b$ are the coordinates of a boundary point, $R'$ is the integration
major radius, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component. The disk
is oriented along the positive vertical unit vector $\hat{Z}$.

This definition applies to an axisymmetric equilibrium and includes
contributions from both external sources and plasma current, rather than
only [external magnetic flux](name:external_magnetic_flux). It differs from
[toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which threads the
boundary-enclosed poloidal cross-section rather than a horizontal disk.

This is the boundary flux-function value, not the axis-to-boundary flux
difference. Together with the magnetic-axis flux, it supplies the outer
reference for poloidal-flux normalization; the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate of the plasma
boundary](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary)
equals unity when those values define the normalization endpoints.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic flux through the
defining disk is directed along $+\hat{Z}$.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description:
Poloidal component of the complex first-order plasma velocity perturbation
eigenfunction in linear MHD stability analysis, projected onto the poloidal
direction in the flux-coordinate frame (ρ, θ, φ) for a single toroidal
Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
The poloidal perturbed plasma velocity is the $\theta$-directed component of
the linearized plasma velocity perturbation eigenfunction
$\delta\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{r})$, obtained by projecting the full complex
perturbation vector onto the poloidal basis direction in the flux-coordinate
frame $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a radial flux surface label
and $\theta$ is the poloidal angle. It characterizes the oscillatory
poloidal plasma flow about a magnetohydrostatic equilibrium for a specified
toroidal Fourier mode number $n$, encoding both the spatial amplitude and
phase variation of that flow component along and across flux surfaces.

The physical perturbation follows the eigenfunction ansatz:

$$
\delta v_\theta(\rho, \theta, \phi, t) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\hat{v}_\theta(\rho, \theta)\, e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}\right]
$$

where $\delta\hat{v}_\theta(\rho, \theta)$ is the complex poloidal amplitude
profile, $n$ is the toroidal mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle
increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $\omega$
is the complex MHD eigenfrequency whose imaginary part gives the mode growth
or damping rate.

The complex amplitude decomposes into its [real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) and [imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), which
together specify the amplitude and spatial phase of the poloidal velocity
oscillation at each point on a flux surface. Alongside the [radial
component](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) and the
[toroidal component](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part), the
poloidal projection completes the velocity eigenfunction and supports
incompressibility assessment and MHD energy partition calculations in linear
stability solvers.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal velocity is directed in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate frame
$(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

items.name: thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Net torque vector transferred to the thermal ion population through
Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange, representing volume-integrated
angular-momentum transfer.
items.documentation:
The collisional thermal-ion torque is the net angular-momentum transfer to
the thermal ion population from Coulomb collisions, integrated over the
plasma volume. Its vector form retains the direction of the transferred
torque; the toroidal component is represented by [toroidal thermal-ion
torque due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions).

The defining volume integral is:

$$
\mathbf{T}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the torque origin,
$\mathbf{R}_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force
density transferred to thermal ions, and $V$ is the plasma volume.

This quantity is the thermal-ion specialization of [ion torque due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions). It describes momentum
exchange, not the collisional energy transfer represented by power.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: flux_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power
deposited on a divertor target surface, independent of how the incident
energy carriers are decomposed.
items.documentation:
Flux at a divertor target is the local scalar surface density of power
deposited on a divertor target surface. It represents the target-surface
load itself, without assigning that load to a particular carrier species,
radiation component, or transport mechanism.

The target-surface flux is defined as the surface-area density of deposited
power:

$$
F_{\mathrm{t}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{dep}}}{dA_{\mathrm{t}}}
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{t}}$ is the flux at surface point $\mathbf{x}$,
$P_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the power deposited into the divertor target material,
and $A_{\mathrm{t}}$ is area on the divertor target surface.

This name is an umbrella for scalar divertor-target deposited-flux
quantities; the explicit energy-load specialization is [energy flux at
divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target). It excludes upstream
fluxes, volume power densities, and signed vector flux components.
Channel-resolved contributions are distinct quantities unless a more
specific standard name states that decomposition.

items.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Signed total linear momentum along increasing toroidal angle within a closed
flux surface as it approaches the magnetic axis, in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total toroidal linear momentum carried by electrons and
all ion species within the volume enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface
as that surface approaches the magnetic axis. It is a linear-momentum
projection, not toroidal angular momentum.

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\psi\to\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}} \int_{V(\psi)} \sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}\,dV
$$

Here $P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the limiting toroidal momentum, $\psi$ is a
flux-surface label, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its magnetic-axis value,
$V(\psi)$ is the enclosed volume, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is
its number density, $v_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and
$dV$ is the volume element. The sum includes electrons and ions and excludes
neutral species. Its aggregation and projection match [toroidal total plasma
momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), while the corresponding
boundary quantity is toroidal total plasma momentum at plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net enclosed momentum points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive
items.description:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by electron-cyclotron
wave absorption and resonant wave–particle interactions, summed over all
wave sources.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net toroidal plasma current attributable to
electron-cyclotron wave-driven current generation. It excludes inductive
current and current produced by other non-inductive mechanisms.

The total driven current is the toroidal projection of the driven current
density integrated over a poloidal cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{EC}}$ is the electron-cyclotron-driven
current-density component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional area in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $dA$ is its differential area. The
quantity is a current contribution, not the absorbed electron-cyclotron wave
power; its broader wave-driven-current counterpart is [current due to
wave-driven current drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: line_averaged_helium_4_density
items.description:
Chord-averaged helium-4 ion number density along a specified line of sight
through the plasma, representing the path mean of local fusion-ash
concentration.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged helium-4 ion number density is the path average of the
local helium-4 ion density along a specified chord through the plasma. It
represents an effective density for that chord, not the local value at a
point or a volume-wide mean.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)$ is the local helium-4 ion number density from
[helium_4_density](name:helium_4_density), $l$ is distance along the chord,
and $L$ is the chord length; $l$ and $L$ are measured in m.

The average includes the local helium-4 ion density along the specified path
and uses uniform path-length weighting. Unlike
[volume_averaged_helium_4_density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density),
it is not averaged over the confined plasma volume.

items.name: relative_humidity_of_detector
items.description:
Ratio of ambient water-vapor partial pressure to its saturation vapor
pressure at the detector, describing local moisture conditions that can
affect detector performance.
items.documentation:
Relative humidity at the detector is the ambient water-vapor content
expressed relative to the maximum water-vapor content supported at the local
air temperature.

It is defined by

$$
RH = \frac{p_{\mathrm{H_2O}}}{p_{\mathrm{sat}}(T)}
$$

where $RH$ is relative humidity, $p_{\mathrm{H_2O}}$ is the partial pressure
of water vapor surrounding the detector, $p_{\mathrm{sat}}(T)$ is the
saturation vapor pressure of water, and $T$ is the local air temperature.
The reported fraction is bounded from 0 to 1.

This quantity describes the environmental moisture condition at the detector
and is not absolute humidity, air temperature, or a detector-response
property. It is distinct from an intrinsic detection metric such as
[spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector), which describes
photon-registration probability rather than the surrounding environment.

items.name: z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point
items.description:
Z coordinate of the point where a sensor is mechanically attached to a
device component, expressed in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame
with z vertical.
items.documentation:
Z coordinate of the point where a sensor is mechanically attached to a
device component is the signed vertical Cartesian coordinate of the fixed
mechanical attachment point in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.
The $hat{z}$ direction is vertical and is aligned with $hat{Z}$ of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $\mathbf{r}_a$ be the position vector of the attachment point and
$\mathbf{r}_0$ the origin of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.
The coordinate is the projection on the vertical basis vector of that frame:

$$
z_a = (\mathbf{r}_a - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{z}
$$

where $z_a$ is the sensor-attachment-point z coordinate and $\hat{z}$ is the
vertical unit vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

Together with
[x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point](name:x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point)
and
[y_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point](name:y_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point),
this quantity locates the same mechanical attachment reference point. It is
not the sensor sensitive point, line-of-sight reference point, or
orientation vector. The zero level is the plane $z=0$ through the origin of
the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame; for a midplane-centered frame
this plane is the machine midplane.

Sign convention: Positive when the attachment point lies in the $+\hat{z}$
direction from the plane $z=0$ of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$
frame.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_state_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle diffusivity is the effective
Fickian transport coefficient for diffusive particle transport of a
specified neutral internal-state population along the poloidal coordinate θ
in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral internal-state particle diffusivity is the effective
Fickian transport coefficient for diffusive particle transport of a
specified neutral internal-state population along the poloidal coordinate
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The neutral state is an
internal population of a neutral species, not an ion charge state or an
aggregate over neutral states.

The Fickian relation for neutral internal state $s$ is

$$
\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\theta,s}\,\frac{\partial n_s}{\partial \ell_\theta}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\theta,s}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
particle-flux component of neutral internal state $s$, $D_{\theta,s}$ is
this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of neutral internal state $s$,
and $\ell_\theta$ is arc length in the direction of increasing $\theta$ at
fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$.

This coefficient is resolved for a single neutral internal state and
excludes summation or averaging over distinct neutral internal states. It
describes diffusive particle-number transport only and excludes advective
transport, sources and sinks, energy diffusivity, and momentum diffusivity;
related broader particle diffusivities include [neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_state_particle_diffusivity), [poloidal neutral
particle diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity), and
poloidal particle diffusivity.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal diffusive particle-flux
component is directed opposite to the poloidal number-density gradient.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Particle-flow velocity component assigned to a neutral species state and
projected in the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame, attributed to effective diamagnetic pressure-gradient transport.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
toroidal component of particle-flow velocity assigned to a specified neutral
atomic or molecular state and attributed to the diamagnetic,
pressure-gradient part of transport. For an uncharged neutral state, it
denotes an effective contribution in a modeled velocity decomposition rather
than a direct single-particle Lorentz-force drift. The toroidal direction is
$hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The toroidal scalar component is the projection of the effective
neutral-state diamagnetic velocity vector onto $\hat{\phi}$:

$$
v_{a,\phi}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{a}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $a$ labels the neutral state, $\mathbf{v}_{a}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the
effective diamagnetic velocity contribution for that state, and $\hat{\phi}$
is the unit vector tangent to increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

This quantity is a component of an effective neutral-state velocity
decomposition, not the total neutral-state velocity and not a mechanical
drift of an isolated neutral particle. It is distinct from the radial,
vertical, poloidal, and field-parallel component refinements and retains
only the toroidal contribution assigned to the diamagnetic part of the
decomposition.

items.name: area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Geometric cross-sectional area enclosed by one winding turn of a poloidal
magnetic-field probe coil, defining its per-turn magnetic-flux coupling.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the geometric cross-sectional area enclosed by one winding
turn of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil. It represents the
magnetic-flux coupling area of an individual pickup-coil turn and is
nonnegative.

For a winding composed of identical turns, the ideal effective flux-sensing
area is

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = N A_{\mathrm{turn}}
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the signed effective geometric flux-sensing area
of the complete winding, $N$ is the signed number of winding turns, and
$A_{\mathrm{turn}}$ is the area of one turn.

This quantity is defined per turn and applies only to the probe-coil
geometry; it does not include the number of turns, winding orientation, or
calibration factors. Consequently, it is distinct from the complete
effective area of a flux-loop sensor, such as [area of a flux
loop](name:area_of_flux_loop). The corresponding [turn count of a poloidal
magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe)
combines with this area to determine the winding's ideal effective
flux-sensing area.

items.name: triangularity_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Dimensionless shape parameter for the plasma-boundary poloidal
cross-section, expressing the aggregate inward radial displacement of its
upper and lower extrema relative to the geometric center.
items.documentation:
Plasma-boundary triangularity is a dimensionless shaping parameter
describing the asymmetry of the boundary’s poloidal cross-section through
the inward displacement of its upper and lower radial extrema relative to
the geometric center. It characterizes the complete boundary rather than
either half-plane extremum alone.

For the upper and lower boundary extrema, the aggregate triangularity is
defined as

$$
\delta = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{R_0-R_u}{a}+\frac{R_0-R_l}{a}\right)
$$

where $\delta$ is the plasma-boundary triangularity, $R_0$ is the
major-radius coordinate of the geometric center, $R_u$ and $R_l$ are the
major-radius coordinates of the upper and lower boundary extrema, and $a$ is
the boundary minor radius. The coordinates refer to the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the entire plasma boundary and aggregates the upper
and lower extremal displacements into one shape parameter. It excludes the
separately resolved [upper triangularity of the plasma
boundary](name:upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) and [lower
triangularity of the plasma
boundary](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), which retain only
one extremum. It also differs from [triangularity of a flux
surface](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface), which describes an individual
nested magnetic flux surface rather than the outer plasma boundary.

items.name: line_averaged_deuterium_density
items.description:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number
density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It is
charge-state-summed over ionized deuterium and excludes neutral or molecular
deuterium and non-deuterium species.
items.documentation:
Deuterium ion density averaged along a plasma chord is the mean local number
density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion population. It represents the
path-length mean of the local deuterium density along the specified chord,
with deuterium treated as a species-level ion density.

The line average is defined by the path-length average of the local
[deuterium density](name:deuterium_density):

$$
\langle n_D \rangle_\ell = \frac{1}{L} \int_{\ell_0}^{\ell_1} n_D(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $\langle n_D \rangle_\ell$ is the line-averaged deuterium density,
$\ell$ is arclength along the chord, $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$ are the endpoints
of the averaging interval, $L = \ell_1 - \ell_0$ is the chord path length,
and $n_D(\ell)$ is the local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) at
position $\ell$.

The local deuterium density entering the integral is charge-state-summed
over ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly
ionized deuteron population. Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium,
and non-deuterium species are excluded. This quantity is a path average;
local [deuterium density](name:deuterium_density) and [deuterium ion density
averaged over the total plasma
volume](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) are distinct quantities.

items.name: total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective coefficient relating diffusive transport of total thermal energy
carried by thermal ions to the spatial gradient of their energy density,
without fixing a direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity characterizes diffusive transport of the total thermal energy
carried by the thermal-ion population. It is the direction-independent
parent of directional components such as the [radial total thermal-ion
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

For a selected transport direction $a$, the effective coefficient is defined
through the diffusive energy flux:

$$
q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)} = -D_{i,E}^{(a)}\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial x_a}
$$

where $q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(a)}$ is the thermal-ion diffusive energy-flux
component, $D_{i,E}^{(a)}$ is the corresponding energy-diffusion
coefficient, $w_i$ is the total thermal-ion energy density, and $x_a$ is the
coordinate along the selected direction. The coefficient excludes
convective, conductive, and explicit source or sink contributions. It is the
total-energy specialization of the broader [thermal-ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: magnetic_flux
items.description:
Magnetic flux is the signed scalar surface integral of the magnetic field
through an oriented surface. Its sign is set by the chosen surface
orientation, while specializations identify the particular surface, field
contribution, or averaging convention.
items.documentation:
Magnetic flux is a signed scalar associated with an oriented surface. It
represents the net normal component of the magnetic field threading that
surface; the flux itself is not a vector and is not directed, although its
sign depends on the surface orientation.

The magnetic flux $\Phi$ through an oriented surface $S$ is defined by the
surface integral:

$$
\Phi(S) = \int_S \mathbf{B} \cdot d\mathbf{A}
$$

where $\Phi(S)$ is the magnetic flux through $S$, $S$ is the oriented
surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the [magnetic-field vector](name:magnetic_field),
$d\mathbf{A}=\hat{\mathbf{n}}\,dA$ is the oriented area element,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal to $S$, and $dA$ is the scalar
surface-area element.

The unqualified quantity denotes the net integral over the specified
oriented surface with no source restriction and no averaging. More specific
flux quantities supply the surface family, source contribution, projection,
or weighting that narrows this definition.

Magnetic flux is distinct from the local magnetic field, from a
magnetic-field component or magnitude, from a flux-coordinate label
normalized from a flux, and from a time derivative such as loop voltage.
[Poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) and [toroidal magnetic
flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux) are specializations obtained by choosing
different surfaces and orientations for the same integral; source-restricted
or weighted quantities, such as [poloidal-current-weighted average external
magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux), retain
the magnetic-flux meaning while restricting the included magnetic field or
applying the stated averaging convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the net magnetic-field projection through the
specified surface is along the chosen orientation of its area element.

items.name: volume_averaged_neon_density
items.description:
Volume average of the charge-state-summed neon number density throughout the
plasma, giving the mean elemental neon content independent of local spatial
variation.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged neon density is the mean elemental neon number density
over the plasma volume. It includes neutral neon and all neon ionization
states, extending the local definition of [neon density](name:neon_density)
to a spatial average.

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ne}} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, and $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local neon number density
summed over all ionization states. The volume integral represents the total
neon inventory divided by the plasma volume. This quantity provides the
numerator in the [neon abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_neon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which additionally normalizes it to the volume-averaged electron density.

items.name: area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Geometric area enclosed by one complete winding turn of a toroidal
magnetic-field probe coil, setting its single-turn magnetic-flux
sensitivity.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the geometric area enclosed by one complete winding turn of
a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil. It characterizes the coil’s
single-turn coupling to magnetic flux and is independent of the number of
winding turns.

For a coil with multiple turns, the effective flux-coupling area is related
to the single-turn area by

$$
A_{\mathrm{eff}} = N A_{\mathrm{turn}}
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective flux-coupling area of the complete
winding, $N$ is the signed [turn count of the toroidal magnetic-field
probe](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), and
$A_{\mathrm{turn}}$ is the area enclosed by one turn represented by this
quantity.

The scope is limited to the physical area of one turn of the toroidal
magnetic-field probe coil; no summation over turns, orientation sign, or
additional calibration factor is included. It is distinct from the
corresponding [area of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and from the probe’s
induced [voltage](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), which
results from time-varying linked magnetic flux. Together with the winding
count, this area determines the probe’s magnetic-flux sensitivity.

items.name: neutral_density
items.description:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms
and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. Unless a resolved
variant is specified, it aggregates over neutral species, thermal and
suprathermal populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated
neutral states.
items.documentation:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms
and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. It is a pointwise
volumetric particle density, not a flux-surface-averaged or volume-averaged
quantity unless an averaging operation is part of the named quantity.

The local aggregate neutral density is defined by the neutral particle count
per volume element:

$$
n_0 = \frac{dN_0}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_0} n_\alpha
$$

where $N_0$ is the number of neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume
element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_0$ is the set of neutral population classes
included by the unresolved quantity, and $n_\alpha$ is the local density of
population class $\alpha$.

For the unresolved name, $\mathcal{P}_0$ includes neutral species, thermal
and suprathermal kinetic populations, internal quantum states, and
parent-ion-associated neutral states that are not otherwise resolved by the
standard name. When only thermal and fast kinetic classes are distinguished,
the aggregate satisfies $n_0 = n_{0,\mathrm{thermal}} +
n_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$, corresponding to
[thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density) and
[fast_neutral_density](name:fast_neutral_density). It excludes ions,
electrons, and any averaging represented by
[volume_averaged_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density).

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
items.description:
Vector of linear-momentum transport rate per unit area for ions in a
specific charge state, with directional projections characterizing
charge-state-resolved momentum transport across magnetic flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state momentum flux is the vector flux density of linear
momentum carried by ions in a single ionization state $z$, combining
convective transport from bulk flow and non-convective contributions from
pressure and viscous stress. It appears in the charge-state-resolved
momentum-balance equation as the flux term whose divergence governs local
momentum redistribution across flux surfaces and couples to electromagnetic
forces, inter-species friction, and anomalous transport terms.

The component form of the momentum-flux tensor for charge state $z$ is:

$$
\Pi_{z,ij} = m_i n_z v_{z,i} v_{z,j} + p_z \delta_{ij} + \pi_{z,ij}
$$

where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state
$z$, $v_{z,i}$ and $v_{z,j}$ are fluid velocity components, $p_z$ is the
scalar pressure, $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta, and $\pi_{z,ij}$ is
the viscous stress tensor for that charge state.

Scalar projections onto coordinate axes are resolved in the component names:
[radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for outward transport across flux surfaces,
toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux and
[poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for the respective in-surface momentum components, and
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux)
for field-aligned transport. Summing over all ionization stages recovers the
total ion [momentum_flux](name:momentum_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when momentum is transported in the direction of
increasing $R$ for the radial component, in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ for the toroidal component, and along the local
magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$ for the parallel component.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the
mean of the two transverse normal stresses carried by their random motion.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the
transverse normal stress contributed by the suprathermal electron
population. In a gyrotropic description, it is the common normal stress in
either of the two field-perpendicular directions.

The perpendicular pressure is the transverse projection of the fast-electron
pressure tensor:

$$
p_{e,f,\perp}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{e,f}-\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,f}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right)
$$

where $p_{e,f,\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-electron pressure,
$\mathbf{P}_{e,f}$ is the [fast-electron pressure
tensor](name:fast_electron_pressure) describing momentum transport from
random motion, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace, and
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the nonzero
local magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

This quantity includes only suprathermal electrons and excludes
thermal-electron pressure, ion pressure, and stress from directed bulk
motion. The factor of one-half averages the two transverse normal stresses
rather than summing them; it does not imply isotropy between perpendicular
and parallel stresses.

The complementary [parallel fast-electron
pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure) is the field-aligned
projection, $p_{e,f,\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf
b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,f}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}$, where $p_{e,f,\parallel}$
denotes that parallel pressure. Together, the parallel and perpendicular
pressures specify the gyrotropic fast-electron pressure tensor, but they
need not be equal.

items.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Neutral particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through surface-emission processes and directed from the wall material into
the plasma.
items.documentation:
Neutral particle number flux emanating from a plasma-facing wall surface
through surface-emission processes is the surface-normal rate density of
neutral particles generated by the wall material and carried into the
plasma.

The emitted neutral particle flux density is defined by:

$$
F_N^{\mathrm{emit}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{emit}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $F_N^{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted neutral particle-number flux
density, $N_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the number of emitted neutral particles, $A$
is the emitting wall area, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the emitted neutral-particle population at the wall
and is aggregated over the neutral particles represented by that population,
without combining them with emitted electrons or ions. It is a local flux
density per wall area, not a total emission rate integrated over the wall,
and excludes neutral particles incident on the wall and the resulting net
wall flux.

This is the neutral-particle specialization of
[particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
It counts emitted particles rather than their carried energy, unlike
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
and complements the emitted electron quantity
[electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
It is distinct from
[incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall),
which describes neutral particles arriving at the wall.

Sign convention: Positive when the emitted neutral particle flux is directed
from the wall material into the plasma.

items.name: parallel_current_density_at_constraint_position
items.description:
Parallel current density at a specified constraint position is the signed
scalar field-aligned component of conventional current density associated
with an equilibrium constraint locus. It sums charge transport from all
charged-particle populations unless a narrower component or population is
specified.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density at a specified constraint position is the signed
scalar field-aligned component of conventional current density associated
with an equilibrium constraint position. The constraint position supplies
the spatial locus or selected magnetic surface to which the value applies,
while narrower quantities may add an averaging or population qualifier.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is this parallel current density, $\mathbf{j}$ is the
[current density](name:current_density), $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit
vector along the local [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field), $\mathbf{B}$
is the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude.

The supported scope is the conventional charge-current sum over all
charged-particle populations at the specified constraint locus unless a
narrower population is explicitly specified. This excludes the unprojected
[current density](name:current_density), other vector components of current
density, and current-density quantities not associated with a constraint
position.

Narrower quantities specialize this parent by retaining the same
field-aligned projection and constraint-position scope while adding further
qualification. For example, the [flux-surface-averaged parallel current
density at constraint
position](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density_at_constraint_position)
is the flux-surface average of $j_\parallel$ over the selected closed
magnetic surface; this parent itself does not impose that averaging
convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the conventional current density has a
component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: radius_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Geometric distance from the center of a circular Bragg-crystal aperture to
the edge of its active diffracting surface.
items.documentation:
The Bragg-crystal aperture radius is the transverse geometric extent of the
circular active diffracting surface, measured from its center to its
circumferential edge. It describes aperture size rather than the curvature
of the crystal substrate.

For a boundary point of the aperture, the radius is defined by

$$
r_{\mathrm{ap}} = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{edge}} - \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{center}} \right\rVert
$$

where $r_{\mathrm{ap}}$ is the aperture radius, and
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{edge}}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{center}}$ are position
vectors in the aperture plane, with $r_{\mathrm{ap}}$ expressed in meters.

For an ideal circular aperture, this distance is the same for every boundary
point. It is analogous to the [radius of a diagnostic
aperture](name:radius_of_diagnostic_aperture), but must not be confused with
the toroidal curvature of the Bragg crystal or its [vertical
curvature](name:vertical_curvature_of_bragg_crystal).

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_hard_xray_detector
items.description:
Signed coordinate of a hard X-ray detector outline vertex along the second
local tangential axis of the right-handed detector-local Cartesian basis
(first local tangential, second local tangential, local normal).
items.documentation:
Second local tangential coordinate of a hard X-ray detector is the signed
scalar coordinate of a detector outline vertex along the detector-local
second tangential direction. It is defined in the right-handed object-local
Cartesian basis $(\hat{\mathbf e}_1, \hat{\mathbf e}_2, \hat{\mathbf e}_3)$,
where $\hat{\mathbf e}_1$ is the first local tangential unit vector,
$\hat{\mathbf e}_3$ is the detector-local normal unit vector, and
$\hat{\mathbf e}_2 = \hat{\mathbf e}_3 \times \hat{\mathbf e}_1$.

The coordinate $q_2$ of a vertex at position $\mathbf r$ is the signed
projection of its displacement from the detector-local origin:

$$
q_2 = (\mathbf r - \mathbf r_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_2
$$

where $\mathbf r_0$ is the detector-local origin and $\hat{\mathbf e}_2$ is
the second local tangential unit vector.

Only the component along $\hat{\mathbf e}_2$ is included. The companion
coordinate along $\hat{\mathbf e}_1$ is the first local tangential
coordinate of a hard X-ray detector; neither quantity is a radial, toroidal,
or vertical component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the
detector-local origin is toward $\hat{\mathbf e}_3 \times \hat{\mathbf
e}_1$.

items.name: major_length_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Euclidean length of the alpha-side of a ferritic element’s oblique
parallelogram cross-section, measured in the poloidal plane of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the non-negative Euclidean length of the alpha-side, the
designated inclined edge of a ferritic element’s oblique parallelogram
cross-section. It is the alpha-side-specific component of length of a
ferritic element, rather than the length of an unspecified cross-sectional
edge.

For endpoints $(R_1,Z_1)$ and $(R_2,Z_2)$ of the alpha-side in the poloidal
plane,

$$
L_\alpha = \sqrt{(R_2-R_1)^2+(Z_2-Z_1)^2}
$$

where $R_i$ are major-radius coordinates and $Z_i$ are vertical coordinates,
both in meters, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The
toroidal coordinate is fixed for this poloidal cross-sectional length. The
quantity is a magnitude and is therefore non-negative.

items.name: implicit_ion_energy_source_rate
items.description:
Implicit ion energy source rate is the coefficient multiplying ion
temperature in the stiff contribution to a decomposed ion energy source or
sink.
items.documentation:
The implicit ion energy source rate specifies the temperature-proportional,
stiff part of a decomposed ion energy source term. It is a coefficient, not
the complete source term or a heating power density.

In the temperature-based form of the ion energy equation, the source
decomposition is:

$$
S_{i,W} = S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{explicit}} + S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{implicit}} T_i
$$

where $S_{i,W}$ is the ion energy source expressed as a temperature-change
rate, $S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{explicit}}$ is its additive explicit contribution,
$S_{i,W}^{\mathrm{implicit}}$ is the implicit coefficient defined here, and
$T_i$ is the temperature of the represented ion population. The subscripts
$i$ and $W$ identify ions and the energy channel, respectively.

The population scope follows the corresponding ion energy equation; this
general coefficient does not itself prescribe aggregation over species or
resolution by charge state. The [total implicit ion energy source
rate](name:total_implicit_ion_energy_source_rate) specializes this
definition to the combined ion energy channel, whereas the [implicit
ion-state energy source rate](name:implicit_ion_state_energy_source_rate)
resolves a specified ion state. A total-ion coefficient is not defined
merely by summing species coefficients.

The implicit and explicit contributions together reproduce the source term.
Their decomposition distinguishes proportional and additive contributions,
not separate physical heating mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when the implicit contribution supplies energy to
the represented ion population.

items.name: radial_volumetric_force
items.description:
Radial component of the electromagnetic body-force density vector, projected
onto the direction of increasing major radius R in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial volumetric force is the $\hat{R}$-projection of the local
electromagnetic body-force density $\mathbf{f} = \mathbf{J} \times
\mathbf{B}$ acting on plasma volumes or conducting wall and structural
elements. It characterizes the net radial push or pull arising from the
interaction of local current density with the magnetic field, driving stress
and displacement in the major-radial direction.

The defining relation is the radial projection of the Lorentz force density
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},
\hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$:

$$
f_R = (\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}) \cdot \hat{R} = J_\phi B_Z - J_Z B_\phi
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the current density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic field, and $J_\phi$, $J_Z$, $B_\phi$, $B_Z$ are the toroidal and
vertical components respectively.

This component is computed in magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium analyzes and
disruption-load assessments to quantify radial electromagnetic stresses on
plasma-facing components, wall tiles, and blanket structures. Together with
[toroidal_volumetric_force](name:toroidal_volumetric_force) and
[vertical_volumetric_force](name:vertical_volumetric_force), it resolves the
complete local electromagnetic body-force density vector described by
[volumetric_force](name:volumetric_force).

Sign convention: Positive when the electromagnetic force points in the
direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: ion_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for ions in a specified
charge state that scales the admissible particle flux relative to its
collisionless free-streaming bound.
items.documentation:
The dimensionless particle flux-limiter coefficient for an ion in a
specified charge state controls the admissible particle flux in the density
equation by scaling its collisionless free-streaming bound. It applies to
the thermal and nonthermal particle populations represented by that ion
state.

The limiting relation is

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}} = \alpha_{p}\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited particle flux for the selected
ion state, $\alpha_{p}$ is this particle flux-limiter coefficient, and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding collisionless free-streaming
particle-flux bound.

The coefficient is resolved for one specified ion charge state and is not
summed over ion charge states. It applies to particle transport only,
excluding the distinct energy- and momentum-flux limiter coefficients; it is
also distinct from the [neutral-state particle flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), which
applies to a neutral internal state. The undirected coefficient is not a
poloidal, parallel, or vertical projection.

This quantity is the ion-state specialization of the broader [particle
flux-limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient): the
parent supplies the same particle-transport limiting concept without this
ion-state restriction.

items.name: ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Signed local volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy exchange for the
aggregate ion population, including thermal and fast ions.
items.documentation:
Ion collisional power density is the net local volumetric energy exchange
caused by Coulomb collisions for the aggregate ion population. It combines
energy exchange for the included thermal and fast ion subpopulations.

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_{a\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the aggregate ion power density,
$\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion target populations, and
$Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate
to target population $a$ from partner population $b$. The aggregation
includes the contributing ion species, charge states, and orbit classes.
This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [power density due to
collisions](name:power_density_due_to_collisions); its thermal and fast
components are represented by [thermal ion power density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [fast ion
power density due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the aggregate ion population gains energy
from its collision partners.

items.name: poloidal_angle_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description:
Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is its angular position about
the magnetic axis in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured clockwise from the outward +R
direction.
items.documentation:
Poloidal angle of a beam-tracing beam point is the angular coordinate of
that point about the magnetic axis in a poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is measured from
the outward $+R$ direction and uses the clockwise poloidal-angle sense in
the $(R,Z)$ plane.

The clockwise branch of the angle is defined by the displacement of the beam
point relative to the magnetic axis:

$$
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left[-(Z - Z_\mathrm{axis}),\, R - R_\mathrm{axis}\right]
$$

where $\theta$ is the poloidal angle of the beam-tracing beam point, $R$ and
$Z$ are the beam point major radius and vertical height, and
$R_\mathrm{axis}$ and $Z_\mathrm{axis}$ are the major radius and vertical
height of the magnetic axis. The function $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ is the
quadrant-resolving arctangent; the negative first argument makes increasing
$\theta$ clockwise when the cross-section is viewed with $R$ increasing to
the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

The scope is the position of beam-tracing beam trajectory points in the
wave-propagation geometry. The value is pointwise for each trajectory point;
no averaging over beam cross-section, path segment, or multiple beams is
implied.

This quantity is not the beam launch angle, propagation-direction angle,
wave-vector pitch, toroidal angle $\phi$, or a flux-surface label. It is the
beam-point locus counterpart of the [poloidal angle of a measurement
position](name:poloidal_angle_of_measurement_position) and uses the same
angular sense as the [poloidal angle of a flux
surface](name:poloidal_angle_of_flux_surface); the distinction is the locus,
not the angular convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the magnetic axis to
the beam point is clockwise from the outward $+R$ direction in a poloidal
cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame viewed
with $R$ increasing to the right and $Z$ increasing upward.

items.name: line_averaged_total_ion_density
items.description:
Total ion number density averaged along a specified plasma chord, summing
all ion species and charge states, including thermal and non-thermal ions.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged total ion density is the chord average of the local [total
ion density](name:total_ion_number_density), including all ion species,
resolved charge states, and thermal and non-thermal ion populations. It
excludes electron density.

$$
n_{\mathrm{i,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $l$ is distance along the chord, $L$ is chord length,
$n_{\mathrm{i,total}}(l)$ is local total ion density, and
$n_{\mathrm{i,line}}$ is the resulting line average. Unlike the
[volume-averaged total ion density](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_density),
it averages along a chord rather than throughout a volume.

items.name: power_of_plant_subsystem
items.description:
Real electrical power consumed by an individual plant subsystem at its
electrical boundary, contributing to auxiliary-load accounting without
including plant-wide aggregation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the real electrical power consumed by one plant subsystem
at its electrical boundary. It represents the subsystem's contribution to
auxiliary electrical load, distinct from plant-wide aggregation and net
electrical balance quantities.

$$
P_{\rm sub} = \left\langle v(t)i(t) \right\rangle_t
$$

where $P_{\rm sub}$ is the boundary real power, $v(t)$ is the instantaneous
terminal voltage, $i(t)$ is the instantaneous current directed into the
subsystem, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes averaging over the relevant
operating interval. For multiple terminals, the boundary power is the
algebraic sum of the terminal power contributions. Positive power denotes
consumption by the subsystem; exported or generated power is not included as
consumed load. The quantity is distinct from absorbed power of a plant
system, total power of a plant system, and net power of a plant system.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density
items.description:
Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the
volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by bulk thermal electrons
attributed to an individual toroidal mode number. It is represented locally
across a poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the rate
at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal-electron
population per unit physical volume, attributed to an individual toroidal
mode number.

For toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local absorbed power density is
defined as

$$
