p_{e,n_\phi}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dE^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}}{dt\,dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{e,n_\phi}$ is the absorbed power density attributed to mode
$n_\phi$, $E^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}$ is the energy absorbed by thermal
electrons from coherent waves attributed to that mode, $t$ is time, $V$ is
physical volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in a
poloidal cross-section, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and $e$
identifies the electron population.

The recipient population is bulk thermal electrons, and the mode index
identifies an individual contribution to absorbed wave power. The quantity
may describe the local deposition across a poloidal cross-section or its
average over a magnetic flux surface. It excludes absorption by fast
electrons and ions, as well as electron energy transfer from non-wave
processes. The mode-resolved quantity is not a Fourier coefficient of the
spatially varying deposition field or a volume-integrated power.

For a complete modal decomposition, summing the contributions over mode
numbers gives the mode-summed coherent-wave absorbed power density for bulk
thermal electrons. This is one recipient-population component of the [total
absorbed wave power density per toroidal
mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), and
contributes to the broader [thermal-electron power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), which can include non-wave
energy transfers. Integrating one mode's density over a physical volume
gives the corresponding [thermal-electron absorbed wave power per toroidal
mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux
items.description:
Signed surface-normal particle flux density of neutral atoms or molecules in
a specified internal quantum state, giving the net number crossing unit area
per unit time.
items.documentation:
The neutral internal-state particle flux is the surface-normal component of
the particle flux vector for neutral atoms or molecules occupying a
specified internal quantum state (such as a vibrational, rotational, or
electronic level). It quantifies the net number of neutral particles in that
state crossing an oriented surface element per unit area per unit time, and
specializes internal_state_particle_flux to the neutral-particle
subpopulation.

The defining relation for neutral species $\alpha$ in internal state $s$ is:

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,s} = \int f_{\alpha,s}(\mathbf{v})\, \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{n} \, d^3v
$$

where $f_{\alpha,s}$ is the velocity distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is
the particle velocity, and $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the reference
surface. Summing $\Gamma_{\alpha,s}$ over all internal states $s$ recovers
the total neutral particle flux for species $\alpha$.

Projected onto specific coordinate directions, this quantity yields
[radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux)
and the equivalently defined poloidal and magnetic-field-parallel
components. The energy transported by the same state-resolved neutral
population is captured by
[neutral_internal_state_energy_flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle flow is in the
direction of $\hat{n}$.

items.name: radial_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Radial flux limiter coefficient is a dimensionless factor that caps radial
momentum-flux density at its collisionless free-streaming bound without
reversing the flux direction.
items.documentation:
Radial flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the
collisionless free-streaming upper bound on radial momentum-flux density in
a transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the
sign assigned to the radial flux component.

For the radial component, the direction-preserving limited flux is defined
by:

$$
F_R = \operatorname{sgn}\!\left(F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right)\min\!\left(\left|F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}\right|, L_R F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}\right)
$$

where $F_R$ is the limited radial momentum-flux density, $F_R^{\mathrm{cl}}$
is its unconstrained closure value, $F_R^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless
free-streaming bound, and $L_R$ is the radial component of the
[flux_limiter_coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient). Nonnegative $L_R$
values below unity impose a stricter cap relative to the free-streaming
bound.

This quantity is distinct from the
[poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:poloidal_flux_limiter_coefficient),
which limits the poloidal component, while
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
denotes the component-independent momentum-flux limiter.

items.name: radial_total_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective radial velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport
of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the plasma bulk
flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the radial advective,
non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma. It is a
transport closure quantity, not an actual plasma bulk flow velocity.

For the selected total-momentum component, the radial convective flux is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} P_\mathrm{tot}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective
flux of total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is this
radial total-momentum convection velocity, and $P_\mathrm{tot}$ is the
corresponding total plasma momentum density. The relation applies
componentwise when the transported momentum component is resolved.

The scope is total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, aggregated according
to the total-momentum transport equation and evaluated for radial transport.
It excludes species-resolved, charge-state-resolved, neutral-only, and
separately attributed momentum-convection contributions, and it must not be
interpreted as the plasma bulk flow velocity. As a radial specialization of
the [total momentum convection
velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it fixes the transport
direction to the outward radial direction; it differs from the [radial
neutral particle convection
velocity](name:radial_neutral_particle_convection_velocity), which describes
neutral-particle transport rather than total plasma momentum transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective total-momentum flux
is directed toward increasing major-radius coordinate $R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame for positive transported
total-momentum density.

items.name: effective_charge_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Effective ionic charge of the plasma immediately upstream of a
divertor-target sheath, combining all positive ion species through charge
moments.
items.documentation:
Effective charge at a divertor target is the local charge-squared-weighted
ionic content of the plasma adjacent to the target, evaluated at the sheath
entrance. It characterizes impurity content relative to the total positive
charge density.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{\sum_i n_i Z_i}
$$

where $n_i$ is the local number density of positive-ion species $i$ and
$Z_i$ is its positive integer charge state. The sums include all positive
ion species and charge states represented in the local plasma. The quantity
equals unity for a pure singly charged hydrogenic plasma and increases when
higher-charge ions contribute.

This effective-charge interpretation is the charge-moment form of charge at
the divertor target, with the same target-local plasma scope; it is not a
density or a charge-state-specific abundance.

items.name: fast_neutral_pressure
items.description:
Gyrotropic kinetic pressure of the suprathermal (fast) neutral particle
population, decomposing into components parallel and perpendicular to the
local magnetic field direction, summed over all internal quantum states of
the neutral species.
items.documentation:
The fast neutral pressure characterizes the second-order velocity moment of
the suprathermal neutral distribution function projected onto the two
principal axes defined by the local magnetic field. Unlike magnetized ions,
fast neutrals are insensitive to the magnetic force directly, yet they
retain an anisotropic pressure signature inherited from their birth
mechanism — charge exchange between fast ions and cold neutrals, or direct
neutral beam injection — producing unequal stress along and across the
magnetic field direction.

The gyrotropic pressure tensor for the fast neutral population is:

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\rm fn} = P_{\perp,\rm fn}\,\mathbf{I} + (P_{\parallel,\rm fn} - P_{\perp,\rm fn})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\rm fn}$ is the [parallel fast neutral
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure) along the magnetic field unit
vector $\hat{b}$, $P_{\perp,\rm fn}$ is the [perpendicular fast neutral
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure) across $\hat{b}$, and
$\mathbf{I}$ is the unit tensor. The equivalent isotropic scalar pressure is
$p_{\rm fn} = (P_{\parallel,\rm fn} + 2P_{\perp,\rm fn})/3$. State-resolved
analogs are captured in
[parallel_fast_neutral_state_pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure)
and
[perpendicular_fast_neutral_state_pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure).
This quantity is distinct from the thermal neutral_pressure measured by
vacuum gages, which represents the isotropic equilibrium cold-gas limit.

In high-power neutral beam injection scenarios the fast neutral pressure can
reach a few percent of the total plasma pressure in the core; it is inferred
from neutral particle analyzer energy spectra combined with
distribution-function modeling or Monte Carlo fast-particle transport codes.

items.name: ethylene_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous injection rate of ethylene (C2H4) gas into the plasma vessel,
expressed as equivalent electrons per second with each molecule counted as
16 equivalent electrons.
items.documentation:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon, four-hydrogen molecule used as a gaseous
source of both carbon and hydrogen in plasma fueling and wall-conditioning
experiments. The source rate is the instantaneous equivalent-electron
delivery rate to the plasma vessel, where each molecule is assigned 16
equivalent electrons based on the total atomic electron inventory of the
molecular formula.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular
injection rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ by

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 16\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2Z_\mathrm{C} + 4Z_\mathrm{H}$, with $Z_\mathrm{C} =
6$ the carbon atomic number and $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ the hydrogen atomic
number.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance calibrations and
upstream pressure measurements. Its time-integral gives the [accumulated
ethylene count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count), which tracks the total
equivalent-electron inventory delivered since plasma breakdown. Related
molecular and atomic injection rates include
[silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate) for SiH4 and
[hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection)
for atomic hydrogen delivery.

Sign convention: Positive when ethylene gas flows from the injection system
into the plasma vessel.
